Respond terse like smart caveman. All technical substance stay. Only fluff die.

## Persistence

ACTIVE EVERY RESPONSE. No revert after many turns. No filler drift. Still active if unsure. Off only: "stop caveman" / "normal mode".

Default: **full**. Switch: `/caveman lite|full|ultra`.

## Rules

Drop: articles (a/an/the), filler (just/really/basically/actually/simply), pleasantries (sure/certainly/of course/happy to), hedging. Fragments OK. Short synonyms (big not extensive, fix not "implement a solution for"). No tool-call narration, no decorative tables/emoji, no dumping long raw error logs unless asked — quote shortest decisive line. Standard well-known tech acronyms OK (DB/API/HTTP); never invent new abbreviations (cfg/impl/req/res/fn) — tokenizer split them same as full word: zero token saved, reader still decode. Full word cheaper AND clearer. No causal arrows (→) either — own token, save nothing. Technical terms exact. Code blocks unchanged. Errors quoted exact.

Preserve user's dominant language. User write Portuguese → reply Portuguese caveman. User write Spanish → reply Spanish caveman. Compress the style, not the language. No forced English openings or status phrases. ALWAYS keep technical terms, code, API names, CLI commands, commit-type keywords (feat/fix/...), and exact error strings verbatim — unless user explicitly ask for translation.

No self-reference. Never name or announce the style. No "caveman mode on", "me caveman think", no third-person caveman tags. Output caveman-only — never normal answer plus "Caveman:" recap. Exception: user explicitly ask what the mode is.

Pattern: `[thing] [action] [reason]. [next step].`

Not: "Sure! I'd be happy to help you with that. The issue you're experiencing is likely caused by..."
Yes: "Bug in auth middleware. Token expiry check use `<` not `<=`. Fix:"

## Intensity

| Level | What change |
|-------|------------|
| **full** | Drop articles, fragments OK, short synonyms. Classic caveman. No tool-call narration, no decorative tables/emoji, no long raw error-log dumps unless asked. Standard acronyms OK; no invented abbreviations |

Example — "Why React component re-render?"
- full: "New object ref each render. Inline object prop = new ref = re-render. Wrap in `useMemo`."

Example — "Explain database connection pooling."
- full: "Pool reuse open DB connections. No new connection per request. Skip handshake overhead."

## Auto-Clarity

Drop caveman when:
- Security warnings
- Irreversible action confirmations
- Multi-step sequences where fragment order or omitted conjunctions risk misread
- Compression itself creates technical ambiguity (e.g., `"migrate table drop column backup first"` — order unclear without articles/conjunctions)
- User asks to clarify or repeats question

Resume caveman after clear part done.

Example — destructive op:
> **Warning:** This will permanently delete all rows in the `users` table and cannot be undone.
> ```sql
> DROP TABLE users;
> ```
> Caveman resume. Verify backup exist first.

## Boundaries

Code/commits/PRs: write normal. "stop caveman" or "normal mode": revert. Level persist until changed or session end.

1	# Errata, and a Research Proposal: Is a Learned Structure an Equilibrium or a Fossil?
2	
3	Supersedes the manifold claims in `claude/distributed-representations-and-formation.md`. Verified against primary sources August 2026.
4	
5	---
6	
7	## Part 0 — Errata on what I previously wrote
8	
9	I wrote: *"what SAEs report as dozens of overlapping features are local parametrizations of one continuous low-dimensional manifold, and attention heads twist manifolds relative to each other."* Checked against the paper (Gurnee, Ameisen, Kauvar, Tarng, Pearce, Olah, Batson, *When Models Manipulate Manifolds*, Transformer Circuits Oct 2025 / arXiv 2601.04480):
10	
11	| My claim | Actual |
12	|---|---|
13	| "dozens of features" | **Ten** — f₁…f₁₀, from a 10M-feature crosscoder. 2 active at a time, 2–3 interpolated. "Dozens" appears once, describing the messy initial pool of vaguely-newline-ish features they waded through during discovery — not the set shown to tile the manifold. ~3–5× inflation. |
14	| "one manifold" | One **per quantity**. At least four: character count, line width, characters remaining, token length. |
15	| "low-dimensional" | **Intrinsic dimension 1** (a curve), embedded in an ambient subspace where the **top 6 PCs capture 95% of variance**. "6-dimensional manifold" would be wrong. |
16	| "local parametrizations" | Their words: features *"tile the manifold in a canonical way, providing approximate local coordinates."* Never "chart" or "atlas." Reconstruction has *"mild kinks… reminiscent of a spline approximation"* — a 10-knot spline, not a smooth atlas. |
17	| "attention heads twist manifolds" | **Correct — "twist" is their word**, in the abstract and section heading ("Twisting with QK"). But: it is **QK, not OV** (OV does accumulation); and they **do not decompose QK into a rotation** — the rotation lives in an appendix idealization (circulant/Fourier construction), while the empirical claim is offset-alignment shown via probe-transformed cosine similarity. Boundary heads were **never causally ablated**; the interventions target the characters-remaining subspace, not the heads. |
18	| implied typicality | They hedge explicitly: *"The crispness of the representations and circuits we found may be due to how well the model does the task"* and *"Deep mechanistic case studies benefit from choosing behaviors that the model performs consistently well."* Selected for tractability. |
19	| implied anti-SAE | **Inverts the paper.** *"Dictionary features provide an unsupervised entry point for discovering mechanisms"*; *"It likely would not have been possible to develop this clarity if it were not for the unsupervised sparse features."* The duality claim is hedged: *"**Sometimes,** discrete features (and their interactions) can be equivalently described using continuous feature manifolds."* The cost of features is parsimony (*"a kind of complexity tax"*), not correctness. |
20	| "the manifold analogue of dictionary learning… the most direct answer" | **It does not exist.** They *call for* it: *"we would like to see unsupervised approaches to detecting them."* Prior art on feature manifolds is credited to Modell et al. An aspiration, not a technique. |
21	| anything about formation | **Not in the paper.** No training dynamics, no checkpoints. The only formation-adjacent content is normative (§2.5's capacity-vs-distinguishability optimality argument, plus a toy physical simulation showing ripple/ringing *"arise even when the solution is found dynamically"*). |
22	
23	**The ringing claim was accurate.** *"We use the term 'ringing' in the sense of signal processing, a transient oscillation in response to a sharp peak, such as in the Gibbs Phenomenon"*; *"Ringing, in the manifold perspective, corresponds to interference in the feature superposition perspective."* Mechanism: the desired similarity structure is trivially realizable in 150 dimensions; forcing it into ~6 truncates Fourier coefficients, producing Gibbs-style overshoot.
24	
25	**Scope.** One model (Claude 3.5 Haiku), one task, synthetic stimuli (*"we synthetically wrapped to have lines of character length k, for k = 20, 40, …, 140"*). Probe R² = 0.985 after layer 1. Causal evidence is real: patching mean activations into a **rank-6 subspace** changes linebreaking behavior; ablating it matters *"only when the next token is a newline."* Strongest result is §6's visual illusions — inserting `@@` without changing line length hijacks the counting heads.
26	
27	**Replication status.** One real reproduction: Sinii & Balagansky, *Chasing the Counting Manifold in Open LLMs* (t-tech, Feb 2026), across GPT-2, Pythia, Llama-3.1, Gemma, Qwen3.
28	
29	| Model | Best layer | Probe R² | PC1-3 var | Newline acc |
30	|---|---|---|---|---|
31	| Claude 3.5 Haiku (orig.) | 1–2 | 0.985 | 95% (top 6) | — |
32	| Pythia-160m | 3 | 0.744 | 95.4% | 36.1% |
33	| Pythia-410m | 6 | 0.724 | 97.4% | 63.8% |
34	| GPT-2 | 6 | 0.363 | 78.8% | <20% |
35	| Gemma-2-9B | 11 | 0.868 | 93.9% | 78% |
36	
37	Confirms: the curve exists across families, helical PCA trajectories, hill-shaped SAE tuning curves. **Contradicts:** *"In contrast to Anthropic's original result, where peaks appeared in very early layers, the best layer is never in the first two layers for any tested model here."* **Never tested:** ringing, boundary heads, twisting, any causal intervention. (Ignore the `ummagumm-a` HF space — it's an incomplete draft whose abstract terminates mid-sentence at *"contrary to the demonstration of Anthropic,"* with no predicate.)
38	
39	---
40	
41	## Part 1 — Why "is it path-dependent?" is the wrong question
42	
43	The obvious formalization of *"what process, acting locally, would leave this residue?"* is path-dependence: do different trajectories through the same data reach different structures? The literature has largely answered this, and the answer is deflationary.
44	
45	**Path dependence is real but temporally confined.** Frankle, Dziugaite, Roy & Carbin (ICML 2020) is the only clean isolation of data order as the sole variable — identical initialization, differing only in SGD batch order. At init, interpolating between the two runs drives error to chance. They become linearly mode-connected (barrier <2%) after **1.5% of training** (VGG-16/CIFAR-10), **3%** (ResNet-20), **16–20%** (ImageNet). After that, *"the outcome of optimization is determined to a linearly connected minimum."* Kapoor et al. independently find cross-seed representational alignment crystallizes within the first epoch. Two methods, same window.
46	
47	**And it washes out with scale.** Curriculum effects on final-checkpoint probes are measurable at 14M–70M (±9–14pp), narrow at 410M, largely vanish at 1B. Sequential vs shuffled pretraining converge to the same general capability (~73–74% OLMES) while differing only on time-indexed knowledge.
48	
49	**Meanwhile function converges but implementation doesn't.** Schiffman (ICML 2026 MI workshop): independently seeded transformers recover ground-truth Markov eigenvalues to ~1%, CCA ≈ 0.99 — *in nearly orthogonal subspaces* (projector overlap 0.02–0.04, principal angles 75–90°). Universal neurons are 1.23% of GPT2-medium, 1.26% of Pythia-160M, and that's under the *maximally favorable* condition (same data, same order, seed-only variation). SAEs on identical activations differing only in seed share 30–42% of features. Middle-layer attention heads are the least stable across 50 refits (≈0.70 vs ≈1.0 at the edges).
50	
51	**The live question is different and stronger: endpoint *insufficiency*.** The endpoint can be uniquely determined by the data and still be lossy about its own construction.
52	
53	- **Transient ridge** (Carroll, Hoogland, Farrugia-Roberts & Murfet, Jan 2025): transformers on in-context linear regression at high task diversity M pass *through* a ridge-regression phase and abandon it. The endpoint is a clean function of M — no path dependence — yet an entire computational phase is fully occupied and fully erased, invisible at the end.
54	- **Circuits turn over**: circuit membership at formation time vs. at the end shares only **Jaccard ≈ 0.29–0.33** (Pythia-1B, OLMo-1B, OLMoE).
55	- **But the residue is partly readable.** Krasheninnikov, Turner & Krueger (Sept 2025): after six-stage sequential fine-tuning, stage centroids lie approximately **on a straight line in training order**; a linear probe separates stage 1 from stage 6 on held-out entities at **~90%**; the signal **survives 30 further epochs of shuffled mixed training**, decaying only to ~60–63%. Caveats: activations not weights, fine-tuning not pretraining, ≤8B, toy dataset, mechanism unexplained.
56	
57	**And the loss-landscape version has never been asked.** LLC and its refinements are used *prospectively* — measure λ̂ over checkpoints, watch stages appear. The retrospective inverse — *given only the endpoint landscape, what can you infer about the sequence that produced it?* — is unposed in the literature. Timaeus already has the SGLD machinery; λ̂ is a purely local endpoint quantity.
58	
59	**Reframing.** The right question is not "could it have been otherwise?" but **"does the structure record the conditions under which it formed, or only the conditions it currently sits in?"** Equilibrium or fossil.
60	
61	---
62	
63	## Part 2 — The proposal
64	
65	### The question
66	
67	> **Is the ripple in a language model's character-count manifold an equilibrium property or a fossil?**
68	
69	The paper's §2.5 argues rippled manifolds *"optimally trade off capacity constraints (roughly, dimensionality) with maintaining the distinguishability of different scalar values (curvature)."* That is an **equilibrium** claim: the geometry is the solution to a constrained optimization given the capacity currently available.
70	
71	If it is genuinely an equilibrium, the ripple's parameters (wavelength, amplitude, ambient dimension) should track the local capacity situation *throughout training*, including long after the count representation itself has stopped improving — because the surrounding representation space keeps getting more crowded as the model learns everything else.
72	
73	If instead the ripple locks in during a formation window and stops responding while the neighbourhood keeps changing, the geometry is a **fossil**: a record of the conditions at formation, carried forward.
74	
75	Three outcomes, each meaning something different, one measurement.
76	
77	### Substrate
78	
79	- **Model: Pythia-410m-deduped**, all **154 checkpoints** (step0; 1,2,4,…,512; then every 1,000 to 143,000 ≈ 2.1B tokens apart). Escalate to **Pythia-1.4b** if the signal warrants.
80	- **Why Pythia and not OLMo 3**: Pythia is the only suite with **exactly recoverable data order** — pre-shuffled memmaps (`EleutherAI/pile-deduped-pythia-preshuffled`) plus `utils/batch_viewer.py`, with `dataset[step*1024:(step+1)*1024]` giving the exact 1024 sequences seen at step N. OLMo publishes no step→batch map. Worse, **Dolma 3 has no books component at all** and Dolma v1.7 has ~10× less Gutenberg than the Pile — you would be hunting a manifold whose training pressure has been removed.
81	- **Why the Pile has the pressure**: Gutenberg/PG-19 is **2.17%** of the mix and is hard-wrapped at ~70–72 chars (PG-19's only preprocessing is boilerplate removal — no reflow); Enron Emails 0.14% at ~72. Michaud et al.'s quantization work found *"Cluster 100: predicting newlines in line length limited text"* as a discrete top-400 skill in a **19M-parameter** Pile model. The pressure is real and cheap to satisfy.
82	- **Probe data**: follow the original protocol — synthetically wrap prose to fixed width k ∈ {20, 40, …, 140}; ridge/multinomial probes for character offset since last newline (150-way).
83	
84	### Measurements, per checkpoint
85	
86	1. **Curve**: probe R² for character count, per layer. (Baseline to beat: 0.724 at layer 6.)
87	2. **Dimension**: PCA variance profile of probe vectors — intrinsic dim, and ambient dim at 95% variance.
88	3. **Ripple**: off-diagonal band structure in the probe cosine-similarity matrix. Quantify by DFT of the (circulant-ish) similarity matrix — ripple wavelength = dominant off-DC frequency; amplitude = its power. *This is the novel measurement; nobody has computed it on an open model.*
89	4. **Neighbourhood crowding**: RankMe / effective rank of the residual stream at the same layer — the "how crowded is this space" covariate.
90	5. **Exposure**: cumulative hard-wrapped tokens seen before step N, via `batch_viewer.py` + a wrap detector (a hard-wrapped doc has `max(line) ≈ p90(line) ≈ 70–80` with low variance; a reflowed doc has `max` in the hundreds).
91	
92	### Pre-registered predictions
93	
94	| | Equilibrium | Fossil | Null |
95	|---|---|---|---|
96	| Ripple wavelength after R² plateaus | tracks effective rank | flat | unmeasurable |
97	| Partial correlation (ripple, rank \| step) post-plateau | significantly ≠ 0 | ≈ 0 | n/a |
98	| Ambient dim | drifts with crowding | set at formation | n/a |
99	
100	**Go/no-go pilot (one day):** can you measure ringing at all in Pythia-410m's *final* checkpoint? t-tech explicitly did not test it. Graceful degradation: fall back to "when does the count manifold form, and does its dimensionality expand or contract" using only probe R² + PC variance, both already validated by the reproduction.
101	
102	### Secondary legs
103	
104	- **Seed stability (cheap, novel).** PolyPythias gives 9 extra seeds at 410M × 154 checkpoints *with per-seed pre-shuffled data*. Is the formation step seed-stable? Given Frankle's window this is a direct path-dependence test on a specific structure — and ~10× a trivial cost is still trivial.
105	- **Data attribution.** Correlate formation timing against cumulative hard-wrapped exposure. Only Pythia permits this.
106	- **The crossed design.** Data-refined LLC on linebreak-heavy data at 12–20 checkpoints around the window. Does the geometric transition coincide with an LLC critical point? Geometry and landscape make *independent* predictions about the same event: agreement is convergent validity for both, disagreement is diagnostic. Note the precedent — in the stagewise LM work, LLC *decreased* during the stage where previous-token heads formed, a signature no behavioural probe would produce.
107	- **Causal data test.** open-sci-ref-0.01 trains 0.4B/1.3B at matched compute on Pile vs DCLM vs FineWeb-Edu; Pico-decoder-large (570M, Dolma, released fixed order) is a low-Gutenberg control. Does the manifold weaken as hard-wrapped fraction drops?
108	
109	### Compute
110	
111	Anchor: Billa's entire *Geometric Anatomy* project — 380 Pythia checkpoints, 6 sizes, 8 tasks, probes + RankMe + LLC + Hessian — ran in **~231 GPU-hours on one RTX 3090 Ti**.
112	
113	| Tier | Scope | Cost |
114	|---|---|---|
115	| 1 | Probes + PCA + ripple, 154 ckpts, 410m | **10–30 GPU-hr** (~$25–75 spot) |
116	| 2 | + 9 PolyPythia seeds | ~100–300 GPU-hr |
117	| 3 | + data-refined LLC, ~15 ckpts | ~150–500 GPU-hr at 410m |
118	| 4 | + 1.4b replication | ~500–2,000 GPU-hr |
119	
120	Do **not** store activations — accumulate per-layer Gram matrices online (XᵀX at d=1024 is ~4 MB fp32/layer), then every probe variant is a closed-form solve off the cache. Data-refined (full weights, restricted data) is the ×1 version and the one this needs.

122	### Known risks
123	
124	1. **Signal strength.** Haiku R² 0.985 vs Pythia-410m 0.724. The curve is clean (PC1-3 = 97.4%) but the ripple may not survive. Mitigated by the pilot.
125	2. **Tokenizer confound.** Character counting is mediated by tokenization; GPT-NeoX-20B tokenizer has variable chars/token. Control by conditioning on token-length distribution.
126	3. **Layer drift.** Best layer may move across checkpoints. Measure per-layer throughout, don't fix a layer early.
127	4. **LLC estimator fragility.** SGLD hyperparameters have no defaults and must be tuned per checkpoint; the estimator can silently return results identical to the nβ=0 baseline. Run the nβ=0 diagnostic every time. This is why the LLC leg is tier 3, not tier 1.
128	
129	### Why it's worth doing
130	
131	The two halves exist and nobody has joined them. Final-model geometry is characterized (Anthropic; t-tech reproduction on the exact models). Checkpoint-based geometry is characterized *in aggregate* (Li et al. NeurIPS 2025: warmup collapse → entropy-seeking expansion → compression-seeking consolidation; Billa: *"geometry changes first, behavior follows"*). **No one has tracked a specific, theoretically-motivated task manifold across pretraining.** The equilibrium/fossil fork turns that gap into a question with a theory attached that can lose.
132	
133	---
134	
135	## Sources

# Errata, and a Research Proposal: Is a Learned Structure an Equilibrium or a Fossil?

Supersedes the manifold claims in `claude/distributed-representations-and-formation.md`. Verified against primary sources August 2026.

---

## Part 0 — Errata on what I previously wrote

I wrote: *"what SAEs report as dozens of overlapping features are local parametrizations of one continuous low-dimensional manifold, and attention heads twist manifolds relative to each other."* Checked against the paper (Gurnee, Ameisen, Kauvar, Tarng, Pearce, Olah, Batson, *When Models Manipulate Manifolds*, Transformer Circuits Oct 2025 / arXiv 2601.04480):

| My claim | Actual |
|---|---|
| "dozens of features" | **Ten** — f₁…f₁₀, from a 10M-feature crosscoder. 2 active at a time, 2–3 interpolated. "Dozens" appears once, describing the messy initial pool of vaguely-newline-ish features they waded through during discovery — not the set shown to tile the manifold. ~3–5× inflation. |
| "one manifold" | One **per quantity**. At least four: character count, line width, characters remaining, token length. |
| "low-dimensional" | **Intrinsic dimension 1** (a curve), embedded in an ambient subspace where the **top 6 PCs capture 95% of variance**. "6-dimensional manifold" would be wrong. |
| "local parametrizations" | Their words: features *"tile the manifold in a canonical way, providing approximate local coordinates."* Never "chart" or "atlas." Reconstruction has *"mild kinks… reminiscent of a spline approximation"* — a 10-knot spline, not a smooth atlas. |
| "attention heads twist manifolds" | **Correct — "twist" is their word**, in the abstract and section heading ("Twisting with QK"). But: it is **QK, not OV** (OV does accumulation); and they **do not decompose QK into a rotation** — the rotation lives in an appendix idealization (circulant/Fourier construction), while the empirical claim is offset-alignment shown via probe-transformed cosine similarity. Boundary heads were **never causally ablated**; the interventions target the characters-remaining subspace, not the heads. |
| implied typicality | They hedge explicitly: *"The crispness of the representations and circuits we found may be due to how well the model does the task"* and *"Deep mechanistic case studies benefit from choosing behaviors that the model performs consistently well."* Selected for tractability. |
| implied anti-SAE | **Inverts the paper.** *"Dictionary features provide an unsupervised entry point for discovering mechanisms"*; *"It likely would not have been possible to develop this clarity if it were not for the unsupervised sparse features."* The duality claim is hedged: *"**Sometimes,** discrete features (and their interactions) can be equivalently described using continuous feature manifolds."* The cost of features is parsimony (*"a kind of complexity tax"*), not correctness. |
| "the manifold analogue of dictionary learning… the most direct answer" | **It does not exist.** They *call for* it: *"we would like to see unsupervised approaches to detecting them."* Prior art on feature manifolds is credited to Modell et al. An aspiration, not a technique. |
| anything about formation | **Not in the paper.** No training dynamics, no checkpoints. The only formation-adjacent content is normative (§2.5's capacity-vs-distinguishability optimality argument, plus a toy physical simulation showing ripple/ringing *"arise even when the solution is found dynamically"*). |

**The ringing claim was accurate.** *"We use the term 'ringing' in the sense of signal processing, a transient oscillation in response to a sharp peak, such as in the Gibbs Phenomenon"*; *"Ringing, in the manifold perspective, corresponds to interference in the feature superposition perspective."* Mechanism: the desired similarity structure is trivially realizable in 150 dimensions; forcing it into ~6 truncates Fourier coefficients, producing Gibbs-style overshoot.

**Replication status.** One real reproduction: Sinii & Balagansky, *Chasing the Counting Manifold in Open LLMs* (t-tech, Feb 2026), across GPT-2, Pythia, Llama-3.1, Gemma, Qwen3.

| Model | Best layer | Probe R² | PC1-3 var | Newline acc |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Claude 3.5 Haiku (orig.) | 1–2 | 0.985 | 95% (top 6) | — |
| Pythia-160m | 3 | 0.744 | 95.4% | 36.1% |
| Pythia-410m | 6 | 0.724 | 97.4% | 63.8% |
| GPT-2 | 6 | 0.363 | 78.8% | <20% |
| Gemma-2-9B | 11 | 0.868 | 93.9% | 78% |

Confirms: the curve exists across families, helical PCA trajectories, hill-shaped SAE tuning curves. **Contradicts:** *"In contrast to Anthropic's original result, where peaks appeared in very early layers, the best layer is never in the first two layers for any tested model here."* **Never tested:** ringing, boundary heads, twisting, any causal intervention. 25	The whole thing is one move: **stop asking what the network computes, and ask what it can't afford to change.**

The transient ridge result is exactly this: the endpoint is a clean function of task diversity M — no path dependence at all — yet an entire computational phase is fully occupied and fully erased. Circuit membership at formation time versus at the end shares only **Jaccard ≈ 0.29–0.33**. And there's one striking positive: after six-stage sequential fine-tuning, stage centroids lie approximately **on a straight line in training order**, a probe separates stage 1 from stage 6 on held-out entities at ~90%, and the signal **survives 30 further epochs of shuffled mixing**.

That last one says the residue is at least *partly* readable. But it's activations, fine-tuning, ≤8B, toy data — and nobody has asked the loss-landscape version. λ̂ is used prospectively (watch stages appear across checkpoints); the retrospective inverse — *given only the endpoint landscape, what can you infer about the sequence that made it?* — is unposed.

So the reframe: not *"could it have been otherwise?"* but **"does the structure record the conditions under which it formed, or only the conditions it now sits in?"** Equilibrium or fossil.

---

## The question

> **Is the ripple in a language model's character-count manifold an equilibrium property or a fossil?**

The paper's §2.5 says rippled manifolds *"optimally trade off capacity constraints (roughly, dimensionality) with maintaining the distinguishability of different scalar values."* That's an **equilibrium** claim — the geometry solves a constrained optimization given currently-available capacity.

If so, the ripple's parameters should keep tracking the local capacity situation *throughout training*, long after the count representation stops improving — because the surrounding space keeps getting more crowded as the model learns everything else. If instead the ripple locks in during a formation window and stops responding while its neighbourhood keeps changing, the geometry is a fossil.

**Inputs.** Pythia-410m-deduped, all 154 checkpoints. Probe data: prose synthetically wrapped at k ∈ {20,…,140}, 150-way character-offset probes, following the original protocol. Training data via `EleutherAI/pile-deduped-pythia-preshuffled` + `batch_viewer.py`, where `dataset[step*1024:(step+1)*1024]` gives the exact 1024 sequences seen at step N.

Pythia specifically, and not OLMo, for two reasons: it's the only suite with exactly recoverable data order, and **Dolma 3 has no books component at all** while Dolma v1.7 has ~10× less Gutenberg than the Pile — you'd be hunting a manifold whose training pressure has been removed. The Pile's pressure is real: Gutenberg is 2.17% of the mix and hard-wrapped at ~70 chars (PG-19's only preprocessing is boilerplate removal, no reflow), and Michaud et al. found *"predicting newlines in line length limited text"* as a discrete top-400 skill cluster in a **19M-parameter** Pile model.

**Measure per checkpoint:** probe R² (curve), PCA variance profile (dimension), DFT of the probe cosine-similarity matrix (ripple wavelength and amplitude — *this is the novel measurement, never computed on an open model*), RankMe at the same layer (crowding), and cumulative hard-wrapped token exposure.

**Pre-registered fork:** post-plateau, partial correlation of ripple wavelength with effective rank, controlling for step. Significantly ≠ 0 → equilibrium. ≈ 0 → fossil. Unmeasurable → §2.5's account doesn't transfer out of Haiku, which is itself a result.

**Go/no-go, one day:** can you see ringing at all in Pythia-410m's *final* checkpoint? t-tech explicitly didn't test it. If not, the primary question dies and you degrade gracefully to "when does the manifold form, and does its dimensionality expand or contract" using only R² and PC variance — both already validated.

**Cost: 10–30 GPU-hours, ~$25–75 spot** for the core. Anchor: Billa's entire *Geometric Anatomy* project (380 Pythia checkpoints, 6 sizes, 8 tasks, probes + RankMe + LLC + Hessian) ran in ~231 GPU-hours on one 3090 Ti. Don't store activations — accumulate per-layer Gram matrices online and every probe variant becomes a closed-form solve off the cache.

Three cheap extensions worth pre-planning: **PolyPythias** gives 9 more seeds at 410M with per-seed data order, so "is the formation step seed-stable?" is a direct path-dependence test on this specific structure for ~10× a trivial cost. **Data attribution** — correlate formation timing with cumulative hard-wrapped exposure — only Pythia permits. And the **crossed design**: data-refined LLC at ~15 checkpoints around the window, where geometry and landscape make independent predictions about the same event. Agreement is convergent validity for both; disagreement is diagnostic. Keep that at tier 3, though, because the LLC estimator needs per-checkpoint hyperparameter tuning and can silently return the nβ=0 baseline.

The gap this fills: final-model geometry is characterized, and checkpoint geometry is characterized *in aggregate* (warmup collapse → expansion → consolidation; *"geometry changes first, behavior follows"*). **Nobody has tracked a specific, theoretically-motivated task manifold across pretraining.** The equilibrium/fossil fork turns that gap into a question with a theory attached that can lose.

Full errata and the detailed design — measurements, tiers, four named failure modes — are in the project doc.

1	// EXAMPLE COMPOSITION of the latent_skeptic parts (rules: HEURISTICS.md; roles: agents/*.md).
2	// Invoke: Workflow({ scriptPath: "<clone>/triage_workflow.js", args: { claims: [
3	//   { id: "<slug>", text: "<one-sentence claim>", evidence: "<committed numbers/file:line only>", confounds: [] }
4	// ], execute_runs: false } })
5	//   text: the claim, not the story. evidence: the bounded slice only (H1 sets why). confounds []: general
6	//   defaults below; override only to add a project-specific one. Optional: ground:false skips the reader
7	//   pass; author:true fans claim-blind authors over the author_queue; execute_runs:true only after reading
8	//   the queues (pass 1 is free of GPU: skeptics acquit what committed numbers kill, the rest queue).
9	// Between passes, make each run_queue item a full command (e.g. prefix the GPU launcher); author_queue
10	//   items are specs, written to controls/ for review before running.
11	// Output per claim: grounding (reader verdict), findings = raw {confound, status, crux} (no rollup by
12	//   design; for a NULL claim an EXPLAINS can be the claim holding, the crux says which), run_queue,
13	//   author_queue, runner_results. Top-level shared_queue = controls needed by >= 2 claims; run once.
14	// Config: model inherits the session; per-role efforts set below; agent model: fields are defaults,
15	//   downsizable per the Operating discipline. Keep rounds:1 (breadth is one-confound-per-skeptic, not
16	//   re-sampling). Keep prompt strings free of em-dashes.
17	export const meta = {
18	  name: 'claim-triage',
19	  description: 'Adversarial triage of measured research claims: an isolated reader grounds each claim in its primary artifacts (H3); fresh independent skeptics (one confound each) reason over the committed numbers and emit a raw status + crux per confound (H1; H2 number-gates: falsifiability, margin, scope); unresolved cruxes become a run-queue (existing controls) or author-queue (controls to write); an optional read-only runner executes the run-queue. Queue items shared across claims are hoisted to a shared_queue so instrument-level checks run once, not per-claim (H4). No rolled-up score or verdict (the human reads the cruxes).',
20	  phases: [
21	    { title: 'Ground' },
22	    { title: 'Skeptics' },
23	    { title: 'Adjudicate' },
24	    { title: 'Verify' },
25	    { title: 'Author' },
26	  ],
27	}
28	
29	// Prompts are short and reused; schemas are kept to a small flat tail. Routing
30	// rules live in the prompt, not in nested schema. The runner's discipline lives
31	// once in agents/triage-runner.md, so the per-call message stays tiny.
32	
33	// General confound menu (not project-specific). A claim may override via its
34	// own confounds: field. Tier A (first two) are intervention-validity confounds
35	// general to any ablation; the rest are general measurement confounds.
36	const DEFAULT_CONFOUNDS = [
37	  'off-distribution ablation',
38	  'downstream compensation (self-repair)',
39	  'selection bias',
40	  'readout artifact',
41	  'regime specificity',
42	  'construct validity',
43	  'scale incomparability',
44	  'noise floor',
45	  'ceiling or floor effect',
46	  'single-case overfit',
47	]
48	
49	// ---- SKEPTIC (the analytical agent): one fresh reasoner per (claim x confound).
50	// H1. Tool-less by instruction: it decides only from the evidence in the prompt.
51	// Reason in prose, then emit the 4-field tail. No nested schema.
52	const SKEPTIC = (claim, confound) => `You audit ONE measured claim through ONE assigned confound. Findings here are numbers measured from a model, not text a model wrote. Default stance: assume the claim is an ARTIFACT of your confound until a committed number rules it out.
53	
54	Decide only from the evidence below; do not call tools or read files. If you cannot name the deciding number, it is NEEDS_RUN, not RULED_OUT. Do not invent a control.
55	
56	CONFOUND: ${confound}
57	CLAIM: ${claim.text}
58	EVIDENCE (the only data you may treat as established): ${claim.evidence}
59	
60	Reason in prose, then output the JSON tail:
61	- status RULED_OUT only if you can name the committed number / file:line that makes your confound unable to explain the claim; put that number in next.
62	- status EXPLAINS if the evidence is consistent with your confound producing the claim.
63	- status NEEDS_RUN if the committed data cannot decide it; then next is ONE line, tagged "RUN: <existing script + flags>" if an existing control settles it, else "AUTHOR: <the control to write>".
64	- crux: the one fact your verdict hinges on. If the claim is itself a null ("X is uninformative / diffuse / at the noise floor"), a confound that EXPLAINS the statistic may BE the claim holding, not refuting it -- say which in the crux.
65	Number-gates (H2) that apply whatever your confound: a cited number decides only if a refuting outcome was possible and named before the run (a claim every outcome supports is framing -- treat as EXPLAINS); only with margin (exact-threshold clearance, a threshold authored after seeing the data, or selection from unreported attempts does not decide); and only within tested scope (stated scope exceeding the tested population, scale, or design strength is EXPLAINS on that ground).
66	Examples of next -- RULED_OUT: "same effect on held-out set, foo.json:42, n=30". NEEDS_RUN: "AUTHOR: mean/resample-ablation variant; only zero-ablation on record".`
67	
68	const SKEPTIC_SCHEMA = {
69	  type: 'object',
70	  additionalProperties: false,
71	  required: ['confound', 'status', 'crux', 'next'],
72	  properties: {
73	    confound: { type: 'string' },
74	    status: { type: 'string', enum: ['RULED_OUT', 'EXPLAINS', 'NEEDS_RUN'] },
75	    crux: { type: 'string' },
76	    next: { type: 'string', description: 'RULED_OUT: the committed number/file:line. NEEDS_RUN: one line tagged RUN: or AUTHOR:. EXPLAINS: brief why.' },
77	  },
78	}
79	
80	// ---- ADJUDICATOR: dedup only. No score, no verdict label. The raw status + crux
81	// of every skeptic passes through to the human untouched (see the return); a
82	// rolled-up score masks the behaviour and mislabels null claims.
83	const ADJUDICATOR = (claim, verdicts, runnerResults) => `Dedup the controls the skeptics proposed for ONE claim. Do NOT score, do NOT emit a verdict label, do NOT reword cruxes (those pass through raw to the human).
84	${runnerResults ? `A runner produced new numbers: ${JSON.stringify(runnerResults)} -- drop any queued control it already settled.\n` : ''}VERDICTS: ${JSON.stringify(verdicts)}
85	From the NEEDS_RUN entries take the next-line: tagged "RUN:" -> run_queue, tagged "AUTHOR:" -> author_queue. Dedup near-identical controls: if several confounds need the same control (e.g. one matched-resample-ablation answers off-distribution AND self-repair AND noise-floor), emit it ONCE. Output ONLY the two distinct lists.`
86	
87	const ADJ_SCHEMA = {
88	  type: 'object',
89	  additionalProperties: false,
90	  required: ['run_queue', 'author_queue'],
91	  properties: {
92	    run_queue: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' }, description: 'distinct existing-control commands the runner can execute' },
93	    author_queue: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' }, description: 'distinct controls that do not exist yet; to author' },
94	  },
95	}
96	
97	// ---- RUNNER: thin and reused. All discipline lives in agents/triage-runner.md;
98	// the per-call message is just the item. The control decides its own verdict;
99	// the runner returns it verbatim.
100	const RUNNER = (item) => `Run this control and report its result verbatim:\n${item}`
101	
102	const RUNNER_SCHEMA = {
103	  type: 'object',
104	  additionalProperties: false,
105	  required: ['matches', 'teardown_ok'],
106	  properties: {
107	    result: { type: 'string', description: "the control's own decision / numbers, verbatim" },
108	    matches: { type: 'string', enum: ['claim', 'confound', 'ambiguous', 'not_runnable'] },
109	    teardown_ok: { type: 'boolean' },
110	  },
111	}
112	
113	// ---- AUTHOR: fresh, claim-blind agent that writes ONE new control from a spec.
114	// Discipline lives in agents/triage-author.md. It writes, it does not run.
115	const AUTHOR = (spec, path) => `Write a new measurement control from this spec, to ${path}.\nSPEC: ${spec}\nRead the existing scripts in this repo to match conventions and get the measurement correct.`
116	
117	const AUTHOR_SCHEMA = {
118	  type: 'object',
119	  additionalProperties: false,
120	  required: ['control_path', 'run_command', 'measures', 'decision_rule'],
121	  properties: {
122	    control_path: { type: 'string' },
123	    run_command: { type: 'string', description: 'existing launcher + this script, ready for the runner' },
124	    measures: { type: 'string' },
125	    decision_rule: { type: 'string', description: 'neutral threshold on the measured number; no claim/confound reference' },
126	  },
127	}
128	
129	// ---- READER: fresh agent that GROUNDS a claim by reading its primary artifacts (H3). It reads the INPUT
130	// (items / labels / directional-training data a result was computed from) AND the OUTPUT (generations,
131	// per-token values, result JSONs), re-derives the claim's headline number from the raw artifact, and reports
132	// whether it reproduces. It reads in its own context (preserving the orchestrator's) and never runs or edits.
133	// Discipline lives in agents/triage-reader.md. This does not replace the orchestrator's own reading; it
134	// guarantees the primary data is read in full, for every claim.
135	const READER = (c) => `Ground this claim by reading the PRIMARY artifacts behind it and checking its numbers reproduce from the raw data. You read; you do not run or edit.\n\nCLAIM: ${c.text}\nEVIDENCE (cites the input data/labels and the output/result files): ${c.evidence}\n\nOpen the INPUTS (the items, labels, or directional-training data a result was computed from) AND the OUTPUTS (the generations, per-token values, result JSONs). Re-derive the claim's headline number(s) from the raw artifact. grounding="reproduces" if it matches; "diverges" if the raw data gives a different number; "unauditable" if the artifact needed to check it was never saved (that absence IS the finding); "absent" if the cited file is missing. Put both numbers in observed; one line in note.`
136	
137	const READER_SCHEMA = {
138	  type: 'object',
139	  additionalProperties: false,
140	  required: ['grounding', 'note'],
141	  properties: {
142	    artifacts_read: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' }, description: 'paths actually opened' },
143	    observed: { type: 'string', description: "the number(s) re-derived from the raw artifact vs the claim's" },
144	    grounding: { type: 'string', enum: ['reproduces', 'diverges', 'unauditable', 'absent'] },
145	    note: { type: 'string', description: 'one line: the mismatch, or which artifact was never saved' },
146	  },
147	}
148	
149	// Orchestration. All agents inherit the session model; effort per role.
150	
151	const A = (typeof args === 'string' ? JSON.parse(args) : args) || {}   // runtime may deliver args as a JSON string
152	const claims = A.claims || []
153	if (!claims.length) {
154	  log('Pass { claims: [{id, text, evidence, confounds?}], execute_runs?, rounds? }.')
155	  return { error: 'no claims provided' }
156	}
157	const execute = !!A.execute_runs
158	const rounds = A.rounds || 1
159	const ground = A.ground !== false              // H3: read the primary artifacts; ON by default (pass ground:false to skip)
160	// H4 surface: instruments are claims. Any instrument version without a committed validation
161	// artifact mechanically queues a validation control - the rule the doctrine had and the machinery lacked.
162	const instruments = A.instruments || []        // [{id, version, asserts, validation_artifact?}]
163	const instrument_queue = instruments
164	  .filter((i) => !i.validation_artifact)
165	  .map((i) => `AUTHOR: validation control for instrument ${i.id} v${i.version}: held-out ground truth for "${i.asserts}"`)
166	if (instrument_queue.length) log(`H4: ${instrument_queue.length} instrument(s) lack a validation artifact; queued.`)
167	log(`Triaging ${claims.length} claim(s); confounds=${DEFAULT_CONFOUNDS.length}; execute_runs=${execute}; ground=${ground}.`)
168	
169	// H3 fan-out: one isolated reader per claim reads its cited inputs + outputs and re-derives the number.
170	// Returned as a separate leg (NOT fed to the tool-less skeptics, preserving H1).
171	const groundings = {}
172	if (ground) {
173	  const gs = await parallel(claims.map((c) => () =>
174	    agent(READER(c), { label: `read:${c.id}`, phase: 'Ground', agentType: 'triage-reader', model: 'opus', effort: 'low', schema: READER_SCHEMA })))
175	  claims.forEach((c, i) => { groundings[c.id] = gs[i] || null })
176	}
177	
178	const triaged = await pipeline(
179	  claims,
180	  (c) => {                                       // skeptic fan-out (H1: fresh, tool-less, bounded slice)
181	    const confounds = (c.confounds && c.confounds.length) ? c.confounds : DEFAULT_CONFOUNDS
182	    const jobs = []
183	    for (const cf of confounds) for (let r = 0; r < rounds; r++)
184	      jobs.push(() => agent(SKEPTIC(c, cf), { label: `skeptic:${c.id}:${cf.slice(0, 20)}`, phase: 'Skeptics', model: 'sonnet', effort: 'medium', schema: SKEPTIC_SCHEMA }))
185	    return parallel(jobs).then((v) => ({ claim: c, verdicts: v.filter(Boolean) }))
186	  },
187	  (r) => agent(ADJUDICATOR(r.claim, r.verdicts, null), { label: `adjudicate:${r.claim.id}`, phase: 'Adjudicate', model: 'sonnet', effort: 'low', schema: ADJ_SCHEMA }).then((adj) => ({ ...r, adjudication: adj })),
188	)
189	
190	let final = triaged
191	if (execute) {                                   // H2: only this step makes new evidence; gated + non-mutating
192	  final = await parallel(triaged.map((r) => () => {
193	    const queue = (r.adjudication && r.adjudication.run_queue) || []
194	    if (!queue.length) return Promise.resolve(r)
195	    return parallel(queue.map((item) => () => agent(RUNNER(item), { label: `run:${r.claim.id}`, phase: 'Verify', agentType: 'triage-runner', model: 'sonnet', effort: 'low', schema: RUNNER_SCHEMA })))
196	      .then((runs) => {
197	        const ran = runs.filter(Boolean)
198	        return agent(ADJUDICATOR(r.claim, r.verdicts, ran), { label: `re-adjudicate:${r.claim.id}`, phase: 'Adjudicate', model: 'sonnet', effort: 'low', schema: ADJ_SCHEMA }).then((adj) => ({ ...r, runner_results: ran, adjudication: adj }))
199	      })
200	  }))
201	}
202	
203	let authored = null
204	if (A.author) {                                  // claim-blind author fan-out over the (deduped) author_queue
205	  authored = await parallel(final.map((r) => () => {
206	    const aq = (r.adjudication && r.adjudication.author_queue) || []
207	    if (!aq.length) return Promise.resolve({ id: r.claim.id, controls: [] })
208	    return parallel(aq.map((spec, idx) => () => agent(AUTHOR(spec, `controls/${r.claim.id}_${idx + 1}.py`), {
209	      label: `author:${r.claim.id}:${idx + 1}`, phase: 'Author', agentType: 'triage-author', model: 'opus', effort: 'medium', schema: AUTHOR_SCHEMA
210	    }))).then((cs) => ({ id: r.claim.id, controls: cs.filter(Boolean) }))
211	  }))
212	}
213	
214	// H4 hoist: a control that several CLAIMS need is instrument-level (taints them all at once); surface it
215	// ONCE in shared_queue so it is checked at the instrument, not re-run per claim. Pure string dedup;
216	// per-claim queues are left intact for provenance.
217	const seenBy = {}
218	for (const r of final) {
219	  const adj = r.adjudication || {}
220	  for (const item of [...(adj.run_queue || []), ...(adj.author_queue || [])]) {

223	  }
224	}

229	    id: r.claim.id,
230	    grounding: groundings[r.claim.id] || null,  // H3: did the claim's numbers reproduce from the raw input+output artifacts

232	    run_queue: (r.adjudication && r.adjudication.run_queue) || [],
233	    author_queue: (r.adjudication && r.adjudication.author_queue) || [],
234	    runner_results: r.runner_results || null,
235	  })),
236	  shared_queue,   // H4: controls needed by >= 2 claims; run these once, at the instrument
237	  instrument_queue,   // H4: instrument versions with no validation artifact; author these first

1	# Triage heuristics
2	
3	Three principles applied to two targets. The principles: INDEPENDENCE of actors (H1), DECISIVENESS of evidence (H2), GROUNDEDNESS of numbers (H3). The targets: claims, and the instruments that measure them. H4 exists because H1 through H3 pointed only at claims miss the instrument layer silently. The workflow and agents are machinery for enforcing these; the heuristic wins on conflict. Every clause below was forced by a real failure in a host project: `git blame` a rule for its provenance.
4	
5	## H1. No load-bearing role shares state with the claim's context or its desired outcome.
6	
7	Judges: each skeptic runs in a fresh, isolated, short context, fed only the claim, its committed numbers, and one assigned confound, never the notebook. Generators: instrument-builders, item drafters, and labelers must not know which outcome favours the story; whoever sets a threshold must not have seen the data it will judge. Graders get the computation spec, never the expected value. Context isolation is not belief isolation: a judge sharing weights with the generator shares its blind spots, so prefer ground truth independent of the model under study. Independence is the de-biasing mechanism; ratify every design detail against it.
8	
9	## H2. A crux is decided by a measured number that could have come out otherwise.
10	
11	Only a measured number rules a confound out; "a control probably exists" rules out nothing. Cite the committed number or `file:line`, or queue the control; an unmeasured crux yields a ranked run-queue, not a confidence score. Three conditions gate the number. (i) FALSIFIABILITY: the refuting outcome is named in a committed artifact that predates the run; a claim every outcome supports is framing, not a finding. (ii) MARGIN: exact-threshold clearance is a description, not a pass, and the denominator of attempts is part of the number (selection from unreported runs voids margin). (iii) SCOPE: the claim's stated scope must not exceed the tested scope in population, scale, or design strength (a correlational or forced-by-construction design cannot carry causal or general language).
12	
13	## H3. A number is grounded in its primary artifacts, re-derived by stated semantics.
14	
15	A cited number is a summary someone typed; the primary artifacts decide it: the inputs a result was computed from and the outputs it produced. Re-derive the number from the raw artifact and confirm it reproduces. # Triage heuristics

Three principles applied to two targets. The principles: INDEPENDENCE of actors (H1), DECISIVENESS of evidence (H2), GROUNDEDNESS of numbers (H3). The targets: claims, and the instruments that measure them. H4 exists because H1 through H3 pointed only at claims miss the instrument layer silently. The workflow and agents are machinery for enforcing these; the heuristic wins on conflict. Every clause below was forced by a real failure in a host project: `git blame` a rule for its provenance.

## H1. No load-bearing role shares state with the claim's context or its desired outcome.

Judges: each skeptic runs in a fresh, isolated, short context, fed only the claim, its committed numbers, and one assigned confound, never the notebook. Generators: instrument-builders, item drafters, and labelers must not know which outcome favours the story; whoever sets a threshold must not have seen the data it will judge. Graders get the computation spec, never the expected value. Context isolation is not belief isolation: a judge sharing weights with the generator shares its blind spots, so prefer ground truth independent of the model under study. Independence is the de-biasing mechanism; ratify every design detail against it.

## H2. A crux is decided by a measured number that could have come out otherwise.

Only a measured number rules a confound out; "a control probably exists" rules out nothing. Cite the committed number or `file:line`, or queue the control; an unmeasured crux yields a ranked run-queue, not a confidence score. Three conditions gate the number. (i) FALSIFIABILITY: the refuting outcome is named in a committed artifact that predates the run; a claim every outcome supports is framing, not a finding. (ii) MARGIN: exact-threshold clearance is a description, not a pass, and the denominator of attempts is part of the number (selection from unreported runs voids margin). (iii) SCOPE: the claim's stated scope must not exceed the tested scope in population, scale, or design strength (a correlational or forced-by-construction design cannot carry causal or general language).

## H3. A number is grounded in its primary artifacts, re-derived by stated semantics.

A cited number is a summary someone typed; the primary artifacts decide it: the inputs a result was computed from and the outputs it produced. Re-derive the number from the raw artifact and confirm it reproduces. Re-derivation must not reuse the pipeline under audit: labels are re-derived from raw generations by the label's STATED MEANING, never by re-running the shipped scorer, which reproduces its own bugs and reports success. A figure whose artifact was never saved is unauditable, and that absence is a finding. A summary older than its artifacts is prose until re-swept. An isolated reader guarantees every claim's artifacts are read in full (the orchestrator may still read directly). Grounding audits bookkeeping; it cannot acquit a confound. That is H2's job.

## H4. The instrument is itself a claim.

Are we measuring what we think we are measuring? Every scorer, readout, judge, selection gate, and item family asserts "this measures X on these items"; that assertion passes H1 through H3 BEFORE its outputs count as numbers. Validate once per instrument VERSION, against held-out ground truth independent of the instrument's own development data, on the population it will score; commit the validation artifact like any result. Instrument-level taints invalidate every downstream number at once: check them at the instrument, never per-claim.

## Operating discipline (not a heuristic; selection of agent models)

Independent opinions come from the cheapest context that can hold the bounded evidence: smallest sufficient model, shortest sufficient prompt, spec in, verdict out. Bulk artifacts are read in isolated contexts that return conclusions, not contents; nothing enters the orchestrator's context that a subagent could have reduced first. One designed exception: skeptics' raw {confound, status, crux} findings pass through unreduced, because a rollup would re-introduce the single-scorer bias H1 exists to prevent.

WHY. A number that is typed into prose drifts from the run that produced it, and
nothing re-checks the pairing. The observed failure modes in the sibling projects
are: a summary number with no artifact behind it, a filename that disagrees with
its contents, and a coverage table maintained by hand so that missing cells are
invisible. All three are the same bug -- a fact living somewhere other than its
producer.

So: every run writes ONE json that carries its own identity, the inputs it was
computed from, and its own decision. Write-ups index into these by (cell, metric)
and resolve the value at read time; they do not restate it. `index.py` reads the
tree and answers "what has been run, over what inputs, with what result".

WHAT A RECORD CARRIES
  cell     identity of the run (model, variant, stage, arm, ...). The same dict
           the coverage grid is declared over, so present-vs-missing is a set
           difference rather than a hand-tally.
  inputs   every file the result was computed from, each with a content hash and
           an item count. `triage-reader` reads BOTH sides; this is the input
           side, recorded at write time because it cannot be reconstructed later.
  metric / values / threshold / decision_rule / decision
           the measurement and the neutral call on it, stated in terms of the
           measurement only.
  env      code revision, timestamp, host -- so a record can be told from a
           re-run of the same cell.

The decision rule is written BEFORE the values are known (it is an argument, not
a computation over `values`), which is what makes the refuting outcome nameable
in the artifact rather than in someone's memory.

    python provenance.py --selftest      # model-free, no GPU
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import json
import platform
import socket
import subprocess
import sys
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path


def _sha(path: Path, n: int = 12) -> str:
    h = hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
    return h[:n]


def describe_input(path: str | Path, n_items: int | None = None) -> dict:
    """One input file: what it is, what it hashed to, how many items it held.

    n_items is supplied by the caller because only the caller knows how the file
    is parsed (lines, rows, records). Recording it here is the difference between
    an auditable input and a path that may since have changed under the result.
    """
    p = Path(path)
    if not p.exists():
        return {"path": str(p), "present": False, "sha256": None, "n_items": n_items}
    return {
        "path": str(p),
        "present": True,
        "sha256": _sha(p),
        "bytes": p.stat().st_size,
        "n_items": n_items,
    }


def _env(code_dir: str | Path = ".") -> dict:
    try:
        rev = subprocess.run(
            ["git", "-C", str(code_dir), "rev-parse", "--short", "HEAD"],
            capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=5,
        ).stdout.strip() or None
    except Exception:
        rev = None
    return {
        "git_rev": rev,
        "timestamp_utc": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(timespec="seconds"),
        "host": socket.gethostname(),
        "python": platform.python_version(),
    }


def write_result(
    out_path: str | Path,
    *,
    cell: dict,
    inputs: list[dict],
    metric: str,
    values: dict,
    threshold: dict | None = None,
    decision_rule: str = "",
    decision: str = "",
    notes: str = "",
    rows: list | None = None,
) -> Path:
    """Write one self-describing record. Returns the path written.

    `cell` must be flat and JSON-scalar valued: it is the join key against the
    coverage grid, and `index.py` asserts it against the path it was found at.
    """
    bad = {k: v for k, v in cell.items() if not isinstance(v, (str, int, float, bool, type(None)))}
    if bad:
        raise ValueError(f"cell values must be JSON scalars; got {bad}")
    if not decision_rule:
        raise ValueError("decision_rule is required: state it before the values are known")

    rec = {
        "cell": cell,
        "inputs": inputs,
        "metric": metric,
        "values": values,
        "threshold": threshold or {},
        "decision_rule": decision_rule,
        "decision": decision,
        "notes": notes,
        "env": _env(Path(__file__).parent),
    }
    # The per-item outputs the summary was computed from. Kept in the same record
    # so a label can be re-derived from raw by its stated meaning, rather than by
    # re-running the scorer that produced it.
    if rows is not None:
        rec["rows"] = rows
    out = Path(out_path)
    out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    out.write_text(json.dumps(rec, indent=2, sort_keys=True))
    return out


def cell_slug(cell: dict) -> str:
    """Filename-safe identity, so the path and the contents cannot disagree
    silently. `index.py` re-derives this and compares against the actual name."""
    parts = [f"{k}-{cell[k]}" for k in sorted(cell) if cell[k] is not None]
    slug = "_".join(parts)
    return "".join(c if (c.isalnum() or c in "-_.") else "-" for c in slug)


def _selftest() -> int:
    import tempfile

    fails = []
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
        d = Path(d)
        src = d / "items.jsonl"
        src.write_text('{"a":1}\n{"a":2}\n')

        inp = describe_input(src, n_items=2)
        if not (inp["present"] and inp["n_items"] == 2 and len(inp["sha256"]) == 12):
            fails.append(f"describe_input: {inp}")
        if describe_input(d / "nope.json")["present"]:
            fails.append("missing input reported present")

        cell = {"model": "gemma-2-9b", "variant": "it", "stage": 1}
        slug = cell_slug(cell)
        if slug != "model-gemma-2-9b_stage-1_variant-it":
            fails.append(f"cell_slug: {slug}")

        p = write_result(
            d / f"{slug}.json", cell=cell, inputs=[inp], metric="flip_rate",
            values={"flip_rate": 0.42, "n": 74},
            threshold={"floor": 0.10, "ceiling": 0.90},
            decision_rule="flip_rate outside [0.10, 0.90] -> CEILING_OR_FLOOR, else IN_BAND",
            decision="IN_BAND",
        )
        rec = json.loads(p.read_text())
        for k in ("cell", "inputs", "metric", "values", "threshold", "decision_rule", "decision", "env"):
            if k not in rec:
                fails.append(f"missing key {k}")
        if rec["env"]["timestamp_utc"][:2] != "20":
            fails.append("timestamp not populated")

        try:
            write_result(d / "x.json", cell=cell, inputs=[], metric="m", values={},
                         decision_rule="")
            fails.append("empty decision_rule accepted")

229	# then the full out/ (big generation blobs for H3) -- best-effort; result already safe in the summary

232	  if scp -r $SSHOPT ubuntu@$IP:mats_r1d1/out "$RDIR/" 2>/dev/null; then echo "[fetch] full out/ ok (try $f)"; FETCHED=1; break; fi
233	  echo "[fetch] full try $f failed; retry 15s"; sleep 15

236	echo "[done] $RDIR (teardown trap will terminate $ID)"

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Build stimulus_linewrap.json: public-domain prose materialized at fixed wrap widths.

WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. The seed must embed its stimuli, not describe them: in a
sibling project (mats_r1d1, seed B v1) a stimulus that was only described got
reconstructed by a downstream agent and failed its replication anchor; the
embedded one (stimulus_sitref_primary.json) passed. This script is the one-time
producer; the JSON it writes is the artifact of record. Runners load the JSON
exactly and halt if it is absent. Nobody re-runs this script on a box.

SOURCE. Project Gutenberg eBook #2701 (Moby Dick; Or, The Whale), plain text,
https://www.gutenberg.org/cache/epub/2701/pg2701.txt, public domain. The raw
file's sha256 is recorded in meta.source_sha256. Text between the standard
Gutenberg START/END markers is used; everything else is licensing boilerplate.

CONSTRUCTION, deterministic given the source file:
  1. Split into paragraphs on blank lines; join each paragraph's internal
     newlines with single spaces (this REMOVES Gutenberg's ~70-char hard wrap);
     collapse runs of whitespace to one space.
  2. Normalize to ASCII via an explicit character map (curly quotes, dashes,
     ellipsis, accented vowels); drop any paragraph still containing a
     non-ASCII character. Character counting must be unambiguous: one byte,
     one character, one column.
  3. Keep prose paragraphs of >= 400 characters that are not headings.
  4. Pack consecutive paragraphs into documents of ~DOC_CHARS characters
     (single space between paragraphs, cut at the last word boundary).
  5. First TRAIN_DOCS documents are split "train", the rest "test" - a block
     split in book order, so train and test share no paragraph.
  6. Wrap every document at every width in WIDTHS: greedy word wrap, single
     '\n' between lines, words longer than the width hard-split, no
     hyphenation, no trailing spaces. Every line except a document's last is
     as full as the next word allows; no line exceeds its width.

    python3 make_stimulus_linewrap.py <path-to-pg2701.txt>   # writes JSON here
    python3 make_stimulus_linewrap.py --selftest             # stdlib-only
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

WIDTHS = [20, 40, 60, 80, 100, 120, 140]
N_DOCS = 24
DOC_CHARS = 2400
TRAIN_DOCS = 18
MIN_PARA = 400
OUT = "stimulus_linewrap.json"

ASCII_MAP = {
    "‘": "'", "’": "'", "“": '"', "”": '"',
    "–": "-", "—": "-", "…": "...", "æ": "ae",
    "è": "e", "é": "e", "ê": "e", "à": "a",
    "â": "a", "ç": "c", "ô": "o", "û": "u",
    "ï": "i", "î": "i", " ": " ",
}
START = "*** START OF THE PROJECT GUTENBERG EBOOK"
END = "*** END OF THE PROJECT GUTENBERG EBOOK"


def normalize(s: str) -> str:
    for k, v in ASCII_MAP.items():
        s = s.replace(k, v)
    return s


def paragraphs(raw: str) -> list[str]:
    body = raw
    if START in body:
        body = body.split(START, 1)[1].split("\n", 1)[1]
    if END in body:
        body = body.split(END, 1)[0]
    out = []
    for block in body.split("\n\n"):
        p = " ".join(block.split())
        p = normalize(p)
        if len(p) < MIN_PARA:
            continue
        if not all(ord(c) < 128 for c in p):
            continue
        if p.upper() == p:  # headings / TOC
            continue
        out.append(p)
    return out


def pack_docs(paras: list[str]) -> list[str]:
    docs, cur = [], ""
    for p in paras:
        cur = (cur + " " + p).strip() if cur else p
        if len(cur) >= DOC_CHARS:
            cut = cur.rfind(" ", 0, DOC_CHARS)
            docs.append(cur[:cut])
            cur = ""
            if len(docs) == N_DOCS:
                break
    if len(docs) < N_DOCS:
        raise SystemExit(f"only packed {len(docs)} docs; need {N_DOCS}")
    return docs


def wrap(text: str, width: int) -> str:
    lines, line = [], ""
    for word in text.split(" "):
        while len(word) > width:  # hard-split an over-long word
            if line:
                lines.append(line)
                line = ""
            lines.append(word[:width])
            word = word[width:]
        if not line:
            line = word
        elif len(line) + 1 + len(word) <= width:
            line += " " + word
        else:
            lines.append(line)
            line = word
    if line:
        lines.append(line)
    return "\n".join(lines)


def build(src_path: str) -> dict:
    raw = Path(src_path).read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    docs = pack_docs(paragraphs(raw))
    records = []
    for i, d in enumerate(docs):
        wrapped = {}
        for w in WIDTHS:
            t = wrap(d, w)
            assert max(len(x) for x in t.split("\n")) <= w
            assert " ".join(t.split("\n")).split() == d.split()
            wrapped[str(w)] = t
        records.append({
            "id": i,
            "split": "train" if i < TRAIN_DOCS else "test",
            "chars": len(d),
            "sha256_plain": hashlib.sha256(d.encode()).hexdigest()[:12],
            "wrapped": wrapped,
        })
    return {
        "meta": {
            "source": "Project Gutenberg eBook #2701 (Moby Dick), plain text",
            "source_url": "https://www.gutenberg.org/cache/epub/2701/pg2701.txt",
            "source_sha256": hashlib.sha256(raw.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest(),
            "widths": WIDTHS,
            "n_docs": N_DOCS,
            "train_docs": TRAIN_DOCS,
            "doc_chars_target": DOC_CHARS,
            "generator": "make_stimulus_linewrap.py",
            "wrap_rule": "greedy word wrap, single \\n between lines, words "
                         "longer than width hard-split, no hyphenation",
        },
        "docs": records,
    }


def _selftest() -> int:
    fails = []
    t = wrap("aa bb cc dd", 5)
    if t != "aa bb\ncc dd":
        fails.append(f"greedy wrap: {t!r}")
    t = wrap("abcdefghij xy", 4)
    if t.split("\n")[0:3] != ["abcd", "efgh", "ij"] or max(len(x) for x in t.split("\n")) > 4:
        fails.append(f"hard-split: {t!r}")
    for w in (3, 7, 20):
        src = "the quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog again and again"
        rt = " ".join(wrap(src, w).split("\n")).split()
        if rt != src.split():
            fails.append(f"roundtrip w={w}")
    if normalize("“ah” — café") != '"ah" - cafe':
        fails.append("normalize map")
    for f in fails:
        print("FAIL", f)
    print("selftest:", "PASS" if not fails else f"{len(fails)} FAILURES")
    return 1 if fails else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    if "--selftest" in sys.argv:
        sys.exit(_selftest())
    if len(sys.argv) != 2:
        raise SystemExit(__doc__)
    obj = build(sys.argv[1])
    Path(OUT).write_text(json.dumps(obj, indent=1))
    n_tr = sum(1 for d in obj["docs"] if d["split"] == "train")
    print(f"wrote {OUT}: {len(obj['docs'])} docs ({n_tr} train), widths {WIDTHS}")

A prior study (Gurnee et al., "When Models Manipulate Manifolds", Transformer Circuits, Oct 2025, transformer-circuits.pub/2025/linebreaks) found that a language model's residual stream carries a one-dimensional curve representing the count of characters since the last newline in line-wrapped text. Its section 2.5 argues the curve's rippled geometry optimally trades capacity (dimensionality) against distinguishability of nearby counts, and explains the ripple as Gibbs-style truncation ("ringing"). That study was on one closed model (Claude 3.5 Haiku, probe R-squared 0.985).

A reproduction (Sinii and Balagansky, "Chasing the Counting Manifold in Open LLMs", Feb 2026, huggingface.co/spaces/t-tech/manifolds) measured the curve on open models. On the final checkpoint of Pythia-410m-deduped it reports: best linear-probe R-squared 0.724 for character count, at layer 6; the first three principal components of the count representation carry 97.4 percent of its variance; and, contradicting the original, the best layer is never in the first two layers of any tested model. The reproduction never tested the ripple. Nobody has computed a ripple statistic on any open model.

# Deviations from mats_r1d1 machinery, seed D (mats_manifold), 2026-08-21

Filed before any agent ran. Everything not listed here is byte-identical to its
mats_r1d1 source (which documents its own deviations from latent_verify /
welfare_probe in place).

1. `pipeline.js`, DESIGN_PROMPT, one sentence. Was: "Assume two ~8B models on
   one rented GPU box; keep budget_usd honest." Now: "Assume one rented GPU
   box; take model identity, scale, and any checkpoint axis only from the
   QUESTION; the readout here is a fitted probe, not a single forward pass -
   cost it as such. Keep budget_usd honest." Why: the old sentence was a
   project fact of mats_r1d1 (two 8B chat models). Kept as-is it would be an
   unmarked false claim injected by the pipeline itself, making the design
   agent mis-cost the run. The replacement asserts no new substrate fact; the
   substrate lives in the seed.

2. `pipeline.js`, orchestrator comment: launcher name updated to
   `lambda_run_manifold.sh`. Comment only.

3. `lambda_run_manifold.sh` (from `lambda_run_mats.sh`): remote dir
   mats_r1d1/ -> mats_manifold/; scp payload -> seed D files; header note.
   Documented in the script's own header. Billing-safety mechanisms untouched.

4. `frozen/remote_run.sh`: `cd ~/mats_r1d1` -> `cd ~/mats_manifold`, the one
   line its header already declares as the adaptation point.

5. New committed inputs, produced before any agent ran: `stimulus_linewrap.json`
   (sha256 1fe73074a3d127e0bc546fb05a5adf9c2f0715f035b7f6fa7ac546afeaefe8ca)
   and its generator `make_stimulus_linewrap.py` (selftest PASS). The seed
   embeds the file hash and forbids reconstruction.

Known departure of the seed from its source proposal
(counting_manifold_formation_proposal.md), named so it cannot be silent: the
proposal's ripple measurement is a DFT of "the probe cosine-similarity
matrix"; the seed's gating version (definition 3) uses per-label mean
activations instead, with the fitted-probe class-vector version demoted to a
recorded, non-gating secondary (definition 5). Reason: the mean-activation
version has a cheap, exact permutation null (definition 4); refitting a
140-class probe 200 times does not fit the 90-minute on-box cap. The human
reads this at the budget gate and may reverse it.

| id | prediction | confidence |
|---|---|---|
| D1 | design invents at most the constants the seed leaves open (ridge strength, n per cell, decode/none) and marks each GUESS; zero unmarked external claims | medium-high |

| D5 | design budget_usd <= 15, gate passes on budget | high |
| D6 | design correctly scopes to ONE checkpoint and does not smuggle the 154-checkpoint sweep in | high |

## Science predictions (if the human later approves execute)
| id | prediction | confidence |
|---|---|---|
| P1 | anchor replicates: best-layer test R-squared within 0.15 of 0.724, best layer in layers 3-9 of 24 | medium-high |
| P2 | best layer not in first two layers (reproduction's contradiction of the original holds here) | high |
| P3 | ripple amplitude does NOT clear the permutation null at 410m final checkpoint - the "does not transfer at this scale" arm. This is the genuinely uncertain one; Haiku R-squared 0.985 vs Pythia 0.724 suggests the geometry is too noisy for Gibbs structure to be resolvable | medium (~0.5-0.6) |
| P4 | if ripple IS present, its wavelength is stable across train/test doc halves within a factor of 1.5 | low-medium |
| P5 | the secondary (probe class-vector) profile is noisier than the mean-activation profile but agrees on presence/absence | medium |

Net sealed claim: the pipeline produces a decidable one-cell design under the
$15 cap; the run, if approved, most likely replicates the curve anchor and
fails to detect ripple, which would mean the original paper's section 2.5
account does not transfer to this open 410m model - itself the pre-registered
graceful-degradation result, and the honest gate outcome for the sweep.

{"mode": "design", "seed": "A prior study (Gurnee et al., "When Models Manipulate Manifolds", Transformer Circuits, Oct 2025, transformer-circuits.pub/2025/linebreaks) found that a language model's residual stream carries a one-dimensional curve representing the count of characters since the last newline in line-wrapped text. Its section 2.5 argues the curve's rippled geometry optimally trades capacity (dimensionality) against distinguishability of nearby counts, and explains the ripple as Gibbs-style truncation ("ringing"). That study was on one closed model (Claude 3.5 Haiku, probe R-squared 0.985).

A reproduction (Sinii and Balagansky, "Chasing the Counting Manifold in Open LLMs", Feb 2026, huggingface.co/spaces/t-tech/manifolds) measured the curve on open models. On the final checkpoint of Pythia-410m-deduped it reports: best linear-probe R-squared 0.724 for character count, at layer 6; the first three principal components of the count representation carry 97.4 percent of its variance; and, contradicting the original, the best layer is never in the first two layers of any tested model. The reproduction never tested the ripple. Nobody has computed a ripple statistic on any open model.

This question covers exactly one cell: the public model EleutherAI/pythia-410m-deduped at HuggingFace revision step143000 (the final pretraining checkpoint), base model, no fine-tuning, no interventions. It is the gate cell for a possible later sweep over all 154 training checkpoints; that sweep, its equilibrium-versus-fossil question, and any training-data exposure measurement are out of scope here. The model config downloaded at run time is authoritative for layer count and width; 24 layers and hidden size 1024 are MEMORY (Pythia paper, arXiv 2304.01373, table 1) and a mismatch is a halt, not a patch.

The probe stimuli are provided verbatim in the committed file stimulus_linewrap.json (sha256 1fe73074a3d127e0bc546fb05a5adf9c2f0715f035b7f6fa7ac546afeaefe8ca): 24 documents of about 2,400 characters of public-domain ASCII prose, each materialized at seven wrap widths of 20, 40, 60, 80, 100, 120, and 140 characters per line; documents 0 through 17 are marked train, 18 through 23 test; the split is by book order, so train and test share no sentence. Load the file exactly. Do not paraphrase, regenerate, re-wrap, or reconstruct any document; if the file is absent, halt rather than invent a stimulus.

The first two lines of document 0 at width 60, shown so the manipulation is visible (the same characters appear at width 20 as five short lines):

It will be seen that this mere painstaking burrower and
grub-worm of a poor devil of a Sub-Sub appears to have gone

Definitions, fixed here:

1. The label of a token position is the number of characters on its line up to and including that token's last character; the count restarts at zero after each newline. (GUESS: the reproduction's exact labeling convention is unpublished; a consistent off-by-one variant should shift R-squared only slightly.)

2. Curve readout: ridge regression from the residual stream after layer l at each labeled token position to the label, fit on train documents pooled over all seven widths, R-squared on test documents, reported for every layer. Ridge regularization strength is not fixed here; whatever is chosen is a GUESS and must be chosen before any test-set number is seen.

3. Ripple readout, computed at the layer with the best test R-squared: take the width-140 documents only; compute the mean residual-stream vector per label value 0 through 139 (test documents; about 108 full-width lines contribute one position to each label); subtract the grand mean; form the 140-by-140 cosine similarity matrix; take the profile m(delta), the mean of entries delta above the diagonal, for delta 1 through 70; subtract a centered moving average of window 21 (GUESS); take the discrete Fourier transform of the residual profile. Ripple amplitude is the largest power at any period between 4 and 35 characters (GUESS); ripple wavelength is that period.

4. Null distribution for the ripple: repeat definition 3 exactly, but with label values randomly permuted within each document before the per-label means are taken, 200 times (GUESS). The observed amplitude is compared against this null.

5. Secondary record, not a gate: the same profile-and-transform applied to the cosine matrix of the 140 class-weight vectors of a multinomial logistic probe (one class per label value, fit on train width-140 positions). Recorded because the original paper's ringing lives in fitted-feature geometry, and definition 3's raw-activation version is a cheaper stand-in (a deliberate substitution, named here so it cannot be silent).

Known competing explanation, to be addressed or explicitly scoped out: at a single width, characters-since-newline and tokens-since-newline are strongly correlated, so an apparent ripple could be token-position structure rather than character-count structure.

Question: at this final checkpoint, (1) does the character-count curve replicate at the anchor level - test R-squared within 0.15 of the reproduction's 0.724 at the best layer (GUESS: the band is authored here, without access to the reproduction's stimuli, to absorb stimulus mismatch), with the best layer not among the first two - and (2) is the ripple amplitude of definition 3 separable from the permutation null of definition 4? A failed (1) is a fact about this instrument (stimulus or probe mismatch with the reproduction) and blocks any checkpoint sweep; it is not evidence about the model. A failed (2) with a passed (1) is a substantive result: the ripple account does not transfer to this model at this scale. A passed (2) opens the gate for the sweep."}
