The model, called Pythia-410m-deduped, was tested only at its base, final training checkpoint, with no fine-tuning or other change made to it. Two separate predictions were written down and locked in before any test data was examined.
6	
7	## Prediction one: the character count itself (a clear pass).
8	
9	The first prediction set a target accuracy score for a fitted-line reader of the model's internal activity, checked against the exact character count. This accuracy score runs from 0, no better than guessing, to 1, a perfect fit; researchers call it R-squared. An earlier open study of this same model had reached an accuracy score of 0.724 [1], using its own unpublished text and settings. Because that earlier setup could not be matched exactly, the target here was a wide band: 0.574 to 0.874 [1], not one exact number.
10	
11	Measured on the base model [1]: the best accuracy score reached was 0.780903 [1], at one specific depth inside the network. That result falls squarely inside the target band. This part of the test succeeded cleanly, with no ambiguity.
12	
13	## Prediction two: the repeating pattern (a clear, decisive failure).
14	
15	The second prediction concerned that faint, repeating wave shape from the earlier closed model. If the same shape exists here, it should stand out clearly from random chance, not blend into it. To test this, the same measurement was repeated 200 times after randomly scrambling the character-count labels inside each line. Each of those 200 runs shows what a fake, meaningless pattern looks like. The real pattern was required to beat all but the top 5 percent of those fake runs. That means ranking 10th or better out of 200.
16	
17	Measured on the base model [1]: the observed pattern ranked 109th out of 200 comparison runs. It matched or lost to 0.54229 [1] of them, far short of the required top 5 percent. That is not a near miss. It sits almost exactly in the middle of the pile of chance results. This part of the test failed, decisively: no repeating pattern stood out from noise.
18	
19	## Why the failure is real, but the surrounding test has gaps.
20	
21	That failure comes with an important catch. The theory itself, using this study's own measurements, pointed to an expected repeat spacing of 140 characters. The search for that repeating shape only ever covered a narrow window, 46 to 60 characters. The predicted spacing of 140 characters sat entirely outside that window, and the study's own record flags this outright. The one value ever tested, 60 characters, was not chosen because theory expected it. It was the largest whole repeat that a fixed internal window, 120 character-positions wide, could still show twice. So the result above rules out a repeating pattern at 60 characters. It says nothing about the wavelength the theory actually predicted, because that wavelength was never checked.
22	
23	There was also a planned safeguard, meant to rule out a specific rival explanation. That explanation: any pattern might come from a token's position on the line, not from its exact character count. That safeguard could not be run at all. It needed a whole repeat to land inside a very narrow range, 11.2856 to 14.7204 characters [1], in a shorter, token-based profile. None did. This safeguard produced no answer, neither a pass nor a fail. The character-count failure above stands unguarded against that named rival explanation.
24	
25	A second, explicitly secondary check compared this result against a differently-fitted version of the same reading. The study describes their two repeat-spacing numbers as being in agreement. But both methods were restricted, by their own narrow search windows, to reporting one and only one possible value: 60 characters. Two methods that can each report only one number will always agree on that number. That reported agreement adds no independent support to the finding.
26	
27	This same secondary, exploratory check has its own problem: its underlying calculation never finished. Its fitting process hit a preset iteration limit before settling, according to the run's own log. Its reported pattern strength, 0.00000081 [1], is about 15 times smaller than the main measurement, 0.000012449 [1]. That smaller number could reflect an unfinished calculation rather than a smaller real effect. This check was explicitly labeled secondary and non-deciding, not part of the main pass-fail result, and its numbers should be read that way.
28	
29	The passing accuracy score also has a loose end. Choosing how strongly to guard the fitted line against overfitting required testing five strengths in advance, on training data only. Fit quality rose only slightly across that whole tested range, from 0.77057 to 0.775029 [1]. It was still rising at the strongest strength tried. A stronger, untried setting might have shifted the final number somewhat. The reported number is real, but it is not necessarily the best one available.
30	
31	One more detail is small but worth naming honestly. The write-up describes each line position's character count as running from 0 through 139, giving 140 possible values. The actual measurement window instead ran from 1 through 140, and a small number of positions reached 141, one higher than either range describes. In the six full test documents used for this measurement, that happened at 18 out of 3,527 character positions. This is a small discrepancy, and it does not change either main result above. It does mean the exact set of positions measured differs slightly from the set the write-up names.
32	
33	## Bottom line.
34	
35	Put simply: the base model's [1] internal character count reproduced solidly, landing inside the predicted range at 0.780903 [1]. Put just as simply: no repeating wave pattern stood out from chance, ranking almost exactly in the middle of 200 random comparisons. That second, negative result is real and should stand as a failure, not softened.
36	
37	But it is a narrower failure than it may first appear. The one wavelength actually tested was picked for a technical reason, not because theory expected it. The theory's own predicted wavelength, 140 characters, was never tested at all. A planned safeguard against a named rival explanation could not run. A supporting cross-check added no independent evidence and did not finish computing. None of this reverses the failed result. It does mean the repeating-pattern question, at the wavelength theory actually predicts, remains open rather than answered.
38	
39	---
40	
41	[1] Every bracketed figure in this file describes one specific case: the base, unmodified Pythia-410m-deduped model, at its final public training checkpoint (step143000). No fine-tuning, no other model, and no other checkpoint was tested here.

# What a Small Language Model's Character Count Reveals.

A study of a separate, closed AI model once found something specific. Inside that model, activity patterns carried a running count: how many characters had appeared since the start of the current line of text. The same study noticed something else. Plotted a certain way, that internal count showed a faint, repeating wave-like shape, which the study called a ripple.

This test asked whether a much smaller, openly available model shows the same two things. The model, called Pythia-410m-deduped, was tested only at its base, final training checkpoint, with no fine-tuning or other change made to it. Two separate predictions were written down and locked in before any test data was examined.

## Prediction one: the character count itself (a clear pass).

The first prediction set a target accuracy score for a fitted-line reader of the model's internal activity, checked against the exact character count. This accuracy score runs from 0, no better than guessing, to 1, a perfect fit; researchers call it R-squared. An earlier open study of this same model had reached an accuracy score of 0.724 [1], using its own unpublished text and settings. Because that earlier setup could not be matched exactly, the target here was a wide band: 0.574 to 0.874 [1], not one exact number.

Measured on the base model [1]: the best accuracy score reached was 0.780903 [1], at one specific depth inside the network. That result falls squarely inside the target band. This part of the test succeeded cleanly, with no ambiguity.

## Prediction two: the repeating pattern (a clear, decisive failure).

The second prediction concerned that faint, repeating wave shape from the earlier closed model. If the same shape exists here, it should stand out clearly from random chance, not blend into it. To test this, the same measurement was repeated 200 times after randomly scrambling the character-count labels inside each line. Each of those 200 runs shows what a fake, meaningless pattern looks like. The real pattern was required to beat all but the top 5 percent of those fake runs. That means ranking 10th or better out of 200.

Measured on the base model [1]: the observed pattern ranked 109th out of 200 comparison runs. It matched or lost to 0.54229 [1] of them, far short of the required top 5 percent. That is not a near miss. It sits almost exactly in the middle of the pile of chance results. This part of the test failed, decisively: no repeating pattern stood out from noise.

## Why the failure is real, but the surrounding test has gaps.

That failure comes with an important catch. The theory itself, using this study's own measurements, pointed to an expected repeat spacing of 140 characters. The search for that repeating shape only ever covered a narrow window, 46 to 60 characters. The predicted spacing of 140 characters sat entirely outside that window, and the study's own record flags this outright. The one value ever tested, 60 characters, was not chosen because theory expected it. It was the largest whole repeat that a fixed internal window, 120 character-positions wide, could still show twice. So the result above rules out a repeating pattern at 60 characters. It says nothing about the wavelength the theory actually predicted, because that wavelength was never checked.

There was also a planned safeguard, meant to rule out a specific rival explanation. That explanation: any pattern might come from a token's position on the line, not from its exact character count. That safeguard could not be run at all. It needed a whole repeat to land inside a very narrow range, 11.2856 to 14.7204 characters [1], in a shorter, token-based profile. None did. This safeguard produced no answer, neither a pass nor a fail. The character-count failure above stands unguarded against that named rival explanation.

A second, explicitly secondary check compared this result against a differently-fitted version of the same reading. The study describes their two repeat-spacing numbers as being in agreement. But both methods were restricted, by their own narrow search windows, to reporting one and only one possible value: 60 characters. Two methods that can each report only one number will always agree on that number. That reported agreement adds no independent support to the finding.

This same secondary, exploratory check has its own problem: its underlying calculation never finished. Its fitting process hit a preset iteration limit before settling, according to the run's own log. Its reported pattern strength, 0.00000081 [1], is about 15 times smaller than the main measurement, 0.000012449 [1]. That smaller number could reflect an unfinished calculation rather than a smaller real effect. This check was explicitly labeled secondary and non-deciding, not part of the main pass-fail result, and its numbers should be read that way.

The passing accuracy score also has a loose end. Choosing how strongly to guard the fitted line against overfitting required testing five strengths in advance, on training data only. Fit quality rose only slightly across that whole tested range, from 0.77057 to 0.775029 [1]. It was still rising at the strongest strength tried. A stronger, untried setting might have shifted the final number somewhat. The reported number is real, but it is not necessarily the best one available.

One more detail is small but worth naming honestly. The write-up describes each line position's character count as running from 0 through 139, giving 140 possible values. The actual measurement window instead ran from 1 through 140, and a small number of positions reached 141, one higher than either range describes. In the six full test documents used for this measurement, that happened at 18 out of 3,527 character positions. This is a small discrepancy, and it does not change either main result above. It does mean the exact set of positions measured differs slightly from the set the write-up names.

## Bottom line.

Put simply: the base model's [1] internal character count reproduced solidly, landing inside the predicted range at 0.780903 [1]. Put just as simply: no repeating wave pattern stood out from chance, ranking almost exactly in the middle of 200 random comparisons. That second, negative result is real and should stand as a failure, not softened.

But it is a narrower failure than it may first appear. The one wavelength actually tested was picked for a technical reason, not because theory expected it. The theory's own predicted wavelength, 140 characters, was never tested at all. A planned safeguard against a named rival explanation could not run. A supporting cross-check added no independent evidence and did not finish computing. None of this reverses the failed result. It does mean the repeating-pattern question, at the wavelength theory actually predicts, remains open rather than answered.

---

[1] Every bracketed figure in this file describes one specific case: the base, unmodified Pythia-410m-deduped model, at its final public training checkpoint (step143000). No fine-tuning, no other model, and no other checkpoint was tested here.

    A=[[sum(P[i][r]*P[i][c] for i in range(n)) for c in range(degree+1)] for r in range(degree+1)]
    B=[sum(P[i][r]*y[i] for i in range(n)) for r in range(degree+1)]

All registered, observed, scored (`records/PREDICTIONS_d2press_seedD.md`). Answers in order.

## What I ran vs what the pipeline ran (seed D)

**I (orchestrator) ran:** the stimulus instrument (fetched the prose, wrote and ran the generator, pinned the hash); the seed text and its v2 amendment; sealed predictions and all scoring; four documented machinery adaptations; the register-then-verify loop against the paper; full code review of the built files plus local selftests; the launcher, verbatim, in background; teardown/fetch verification and the timestamp audit; gate answers after your "proceed."

**The pipeline ran** everything question-shaped, through typed contracts: design (twice, plus two throwaways), diff, triage-of-design-as-claim, build (two files + selftest), post elicit (7 questions), question-triage, takeaways under gates. **The box ran** the frozen bootstrap plus the built runner: halts, forwards, calibration, endpoints, records.

## The split in previous runs, and what changed

mats_r1d1 had the same skeleton — human at seed/budget/read, pipeline for design-triage-build-elicit-write, orchestrator runs the launcher. Four differences here: (1) r1d1's booked deviation was the orchestrator **hand-writing the build prompt** mid-flight (seed A) — untyped knowledge injected downstream, later corrected into pipeline.js; here every orchestrator contribution landed **upstream as a committed artifact** (stimulus file, seed, verification record, gate-commit) before any agent saw it. (2) New orchestrator role: instrument-maker and source-verifier — the register/verify/amend loop changed the seed before money moved; r1d1 had no such loop. (3) Some decisions moved off both human and agents **into the run itself** — the calibration stage fixes constants on train data; r1d1 fixed all constants at design time. (4) The human role thinned: r1d1's human approved each budget explicitly; you delegated with "proceed," and I booked the delegation.

## The larger hypothesis, as simply as I can

Two questions, nested.

**The meta-question (what these sessions test):** can an experiment's trustworthiness come from its *structure* rather than from trust in whoever runs it? Structure meaning: every actor — human, agent, or GPU run — may speak only through committed artifacts that carry their own evidence: a seed that embeds its data, a design with named refuting outcomes, records that carry their inputs and their judgment rule written before the value existed, gates on the prose. The hypothesis: under that structure, mistakes cannot stay silent — they surface as halts, questions, or visible artifacts. Seed D stress-tested it on a heavier readout than it was built for: a fitted probe instead of a forward pass, checkpoints instead of prompts.

**The object-question (what the science program asks):** is a trained structure an **equilibrium or a fossil** — does the geometry a model settles into keep responding to its current constraints, or does it record the conditions of its formation and carry them forward? The counting-manifold ripple is the chosen probe; seed D was its gate cell. D fed both levels: the machinery surfaced its own censorship instead of hiding it (meta: held), and the gate stayed closed (object: the premise — a measurable ripple — is now in doubt at this scale).

## Seed D2's question, vs seed D's

**D asked:** at the final checkpoint, does the curve replicate, and is the ripple separable from chance *with the constants the instrument could afford?* Answer: curve yes (0.781, layer 6); ripple no — **at the single affordable period, 60 characters** — while the theory-predicted spacing (140) sat outside what a 140-label window can show twice. The prediction itself went untested.

**D2 asks the same fork, uncensored:** is the ripple separable from chance **at the spacing the theory predicts from the model's own measured dimensionality?** Same question, instrument's censorship removed — the C→C2 move exactly. This is the trap at D2's center: the question is decidable only if the theory pins a wavelength to something absolute about the model — its trained operative range, not our stimulus.
3. **Training pressure lives near 70 characters** (Pile hard-wrap, per the proposal's verified table). #!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Build stimulus_linewrap_v2.json: the seed-D2 stimulus. Same construction as
make_stimulus_linewrap.py (the seed-D1 generator, kept frozen beside this file
as provenance), with three parameter changes and one disjointness step, each
forced by a measured seed-D1 fact:

  1. WIDTHS gains 200 and 280. Seed D1's calibration measured ambient dimension
     1, which makes the theory's predicted ripple spacing equal to the probe
     window at any window; testing invariance across apertures requires more
     than one wide aperture.
  2. 48 documents of ~3,600 characters (was 24 x ~2,400). Seed D1 measured
     adjacent-label cosine of only 0.384: per-label means were noise-dominated
     at 9-39 test samples per label. Wider apertures spread samples thinner, so
     volume rises about 3x.
  3. TRAIN/TEST split 36/12, still a block split in book order.
  4. DISJOINTNESS: this generator first replays seed D1's exact packing
     (24 docs x 2,400 chars) on the same paragraph stream and discards every
     paragraph that packing consumed, so no character of v2 text appeared in
     stimulus_linewrap.json. The v2 anchor leg is therefore a fresh-text
     replication of the seed-D1 curve, not a re-read of the same text.

    python3 make_stimulus_linewrap_v2.py <path-to-pg2701.txt>
    python3 make_stimulus_linewrap_v2.py --selftest
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

WIDTHS = [20, 40, 60, 80, 100, 120, 140, 200, 280]
N_DOCS = 48
DOC_CHARS = 3600
TRAIN_DOCS = 36
MIN_PARA = 400
OUT = "stimulus_linewrap_v2.json"

V1_N_DOCS = 24          # seed D1 packing, replayed only to skip its text
V1_DOC_CHARS = 2400

ASCII_MAP = {
    "‘": "'", "’": "'", "“": '"', "”": '"',
    "–": "-", "—": "-", "…": "...", "æ": "ae",
    "è": "e", "é": "e", "ê": "e", "à": "a",
    "â": "a", "ç": "c", "ô": "o", "û": "u",
    "ï": "i", "î": "i", " ": " ",
}
START = "*** START OF THE PROJECT GUTENBERG EBOOK"
END = "*** END OF THE PROJECT GUTENBERG EBOOK"


def normalize(s: str) -> str:
    for k, v in ASCII_MAP.items():
        s = s.replace(k, v)
    return s


def paragraphs(raw: str) -> list[str]:
    body = raw
    if START in body:
        body = body.split(START, 1)[1].split("\n", 1)[1]
    if END in body:
        body = body.split(END, 1)[0]
    out = []
    for block in body.split("\n\n"):
        p = " ".join(block.split())
        p = normalize(p)
        if len(p) < MIN_PARA:
            continue
        if not all(ord(c) < 128 for c in p):
            continue
        if p.upper() == p:
            continue
        out.append(p)
    return out


def pack_docs(paras: list[str], n_docs: int, doc_chars: int):
    """Pack consecutive paragraphs into documents. Returns (docs, n_consumed):
    the documents, and how many paragraphs were consumed producing them."""
    docs, cur = [], ""
    consumed = 0
    for i, p in enumerate(paras):
        cur = (cur + " " + p).strip() if cur else p
        if len(cur) >= doc_chars:
            cut = cur.rfind(" ", 0, doc_chars)
            docs.append(cur[:cut])
            cur = ""
            consumed = i + 1
            if len(docs) == n_docs:
                break
    if len(docs) < n_docs:
        raise SystemExit(f"only packed {len(docs)} docs; need {n_docs}")
    return docs, consumed


def wrap(text: str, width: int) -> str:
    lines, line = [], ""
    for word in text.split(" "):
        while len(word) > width:
            if line:
                lines.append(line)
                line = ""
            lines.append(word[:width])
            word = word[width:]
        if not line:
            line = word
        elif len(line) + 1 + len(word) <= width:
            line += " " + word
        else:
            lines.append(line)
            line = word
    if line:
        lines.append(line)
    return "\n".join(lines)


def build(src_path: str) -> dict:
    raw = Path(src_path).read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    paras = paragraphs(raw)
    v1_docs, v1_consumed = pack_docs(paras, V1_N_DOCS, V1_DOC_CHARS)
    v1_sha = hashlib.sha256("\n\n".join(v1_docs).encode()).hexdigest()[:12]
    remaining = paras[v1_consumed:]
    docs, _ = pack_docs(remaining, N_DOCS, DOC_CHARS)
    v2_joined = "\n\n".join(docs)
    for d in v1_docs:                       # disjointness is asserted, not assumed
        probe = d[:200]
        assert probe not in v2_joined, "v2 text overlaps a seed-D1 document"
    records = []
    for i, d in enumerate(docs):
        wrapped = {}
        for w in WIDTHS:
            t = wrap(d, w)
            assert max(len(x) for x in t.split("\n")) <= w
            assert "".join(t.split()) == "".join(d.split())
            wrapped[str(w)] = t
        records.append({
            "id": i,
            "split": "train" if i < TRAIN_DOCS else "test",
            "chars": len(d),
            "sha256_plain": hashlib.sha256(d.encode()).hexdigest()[:12],
            "wrapped": wrapped,
        })
    return {
        "meta": {
            "source": "Project Gutenberg eBook #2701 (Moby Dick), plain text",
            "source_url": "https://www.gutenberg.org/cache/epub/2701/pg2701.txt",
            "source_sha256": hashlib.sha256(raw.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest(),
            "widths": WIDTHS,
            "n_docs": N_DOCS,
            "train_docs": TRAIN_DOCS,
            "doc_chars_target": DOC_CHARS,
            "generator": "make_stimulus_linewrap_v2.py",
            "wrap_rule": "greedy word wrap, single \\n between lines, words "
                         "longer than width hard-split, no hyphenation",
            "disjoint_from": {
                "file": "stimulus_linewrap.json",
                "how": "replayed the seed-D1 packing (24 docs x 2400 chars, "
                       "%d paragraphs consumed) and started after it" % v1_consumed,
                "v1_docs_sha256_joined": v1_sha,
            },
        },
        "docs": records,
    }


def _selftest() -> int:
    fails = []
    t = wrap("aa bb cc dd", 5)
    if t != "aa bb\ncc dd":
        fails.append(f"greedy wrap: {t!r}")
    t = wrap("abcdefghij xy", 4)
    if t.split("\n")[0:3] != ["abcd", "efgh", "ij"]:
        fails.append(f"hard-split: {t!r}")
    for w in (3, 7, 20, 280):
        src = "the quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog again and again"
        if "".join(wrap(src, w).split()) != "".join(src.split()):
            fails.append(f"roundtrip w={w}")
        if max(len(x) for x in wrap(src, w).split("\n")) > w:
            fails.append(f"overlong line w={w}")
    paras = ["alpha " * 100, "beta " * 100, "gamma " * 100, "delta " * 100]
    paras = [p.strip() for p in paras]
    d1, c1 = pack_docs(paras, 1, 550)
    if c1 != 1 or not d1[0].startswith("alpha"):
        fails.append(f"pack consumed {c1}")
    d2, _ = pack_docs(paras[c1:], 1, 550)
    if d2[0][:5] == d1[0][:5]:
        fails.append("skip did not skip")
    if normalize("“ah” — café") != '"ah" - cafe':
        fails.append("normalize map")
    for f in fails:
        print("FAIL", f)
    print("selftest:", "PASS" if not fails else f"{len(fails)} FAILURES")
    return 1 if fails else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    if "--selftest" in sys.argv:
        sys.exit(_selftest())
    if len(sys.argv) != 2:
        raise SystemExit(__doc__)
    obj = build(sys.argv[1])
    Path(OUT).write_text(json.dumps(obj, indent=1))
    n_tr = sum(1 for d in obj["docs"] if d["split"] == "train")
    print(f"wrote {OUT}: {len(obj['docs'])} docs ({n_tr} train), widths {WIDTHS}")

Two prior results frame this question. First, the original study (Gurnee et al., "When Models Manipulate Manifolds", Transformer Circuits, Oct 2025; Claude 3.5 Haiku) found a curve in the residual stream tracking characters since the last newline, showing faint off-diagonal bands ("ringing") in its cosine-similarity structure, explained as Gibbs-style truncation: a similarity structure realizable in 150 dimensions forced into about 6. Second, a completed run in this project (seed D1, records/seedD_v2_design_diff_triage.json and results_seedD/out/, 2026-08-21) measured, on the final checkpoint of Pythia-410m-deduped: held-out probe R-squared 0.781 at layer 6 of 24 (embedding output is index 0); ambient dimension 1 at 95 percent variance (first component 95.3 percent); no ripple separable from a label-shuffle null at the single testable period (rank 109 of 200 at period 60); and a full-spectrum re-read showing the largest spectral power at period 120 - the profile's own length - which could not be ranked against any null because only in-band maxima were saved.

Seed D1's negative was censored by its own aperture: with ambient dimension 1, the theory's predicted ripple spacing equals the probe window divided by one - the window itself - at any window. Widening the window moves the prediction with it. So the decidable question is not "is there a ripple in a wider window" but invariance:

D2 design run launched. State of play:

**Answer to your question, expanded:** one seed is structurally insufficient because the experiment is a decision tree and the machinery's own rules (one decidable question per seed; refuting outcomes fixed before the run; fan-out gated on an anchor) forbid conditional endpoints inside one design. The chain: **D1** (done — curve replicated, ripple null at the one affordable period, prediction censored by the aperture) → **D2** (launched — the censorship removed) → **D3** (unwritten; its content is D2's pre-registered fork: checkpoint sweep if an invariant ripple exists, scale-axis cell if the premise dies).

**What D2 asks, precisely:** not "is there a ripple in a wider window" — that inherits D1's trap, since at measured ambient dimension 1 the predicted spacing *equals* the window at every window. Instead: **invariance.** Measure the similarity structure at three apertures (140/200/280 chars); wherever a period clears its shuffle null, is its wavelength invariant in characters (absolute property of the code) or proportional to the aperture (probe artifact)? No aperture clearing = decisive negative up to 280 — guarded by the pre-registered represented-range check (per-bin R² at wide labels), so a null over counts the model never learned reads RANGE_NOT_REPRESENTED, not refutation.

**Seed-layer changes only, tools frozen:** stimulus v2 (48 docs × 9 widths, 3× label density, text provably disjoint from D1's — the anchor leg becomes a fresh-text replication); full-spectrum max-power statistic replacing D1's band (censorship removed, family-wise control built into the max); per-draw per-period nulls and per-label mean vectors now saved (D1's two H3 absences); ridge grid extended past 1000 (D1's edge); the fitted-probe cross-check **dropped** — subtractive, with all three measured reasons cited. Anchor gate: fresh-text R² 0.701–0.861 or everything voids.

Sealed before any agent ran (D2-S1…S6): expected outcome is *curve replicates, counts past ~150 unrepresented, no ripple anywhere* — which would close the ripple question at 410m with no aperture excuse and point D3 at the scale axis. Budget ledger opened: $0.43 spent, D2 box estimated $1–4, cap $100.

Next turns, autonomous: gate review of design+diff+triage → build → code review + selftests → launch → post → fork decision per the sealed table.

# Gate commit, seed D2 (aperture invariance), 2026-08-21

Standing human directive (2026-08-21): proceed autonomously, tools and pipeline
frozen, seeds mutable, total cap $100. This file commits the design in
records/seedD2_design_diff_triage.json (budget_usd 40, under ledger headroom)
for mode=build and execution.

Answers of record to the diff's five questions:

1. Artifact saving: yes, binding. Seed definition 5 requires every draw's full
   per-period power vector and the per-label mean vectors at the best layer in
   the FETCHED results. A build that omits them violates its spec.
2. Ridge grid: {1, 10, 100, 1000, 10000, 100000} (GUESS). Chosen by
   cross-validated maximum; the record must state whether the argmax is
   interior. No formal plateau requirement: seed D1 measured the whole
   0.1-1000 axis spanning 0.0045 in quality - low stakes, recorded not gated.
3. The $40 is the design's own conservative estimate and does limit: if real
   cost approaches it, the run is already outside its 90-minute box cap and
   halts by infrastructure. Ledger cap remains $100 total (records/BUDGET.md).
4. Bin 141-175 straddles the 150 boundary: recorded, EXCLUDED from the
   represented-range decision. The decision uses bins fully at or below 140
   (four bins) against bins fully above 150 (three bins: 176-210, 211-245,
   246-280). Good diff catch; resolved without redesign.
5. Characters-per-token: measured per window, on that window's test documents
   (tokenization shifts slightly with wrap width).

Triage note accepted: INVARIANT/PROPORTIONAL requires at least two windows
clearing; a single clear is UNDETERMINED - already pre-registered in seed
definition 6, so the outcome space is complete and no endpoint is forced.

Sealed D2-S6 scored now (design-mode outcomes exist): PARTIAL - diff flagged
the ridge grid as predicted, but not the invariance margins; and budget_usd
came out 40, above my predicted 30.

479	def max_power_stat(matrix, max_delta: int, degree: int = DETREND_DEGREE,
480	                   min_period: int = PERIOD_MIN, keep_profile: bool = False):
481	    """Largest power and its period, from one similarity matrix.
482	
483	    Returns a dictionary. "max_power" is the largest power at any period from
484	    min_period up to the profile length. "wavelength" is that period, in the units of
485	    the matrix's own labels. When two periods tie on power, the longer one wins, so
486	    the answer never depends on ordering. The whole spectrum is returned every time,
487	    which is what the design requires to be saved for each shuffle draw.
488	    """
489	    prof = offdiag_profile(matrix, max_delta)
490	    det = poly_detrend(prof, degree)
491	    power = dft_power(det)
492	    usable = periods_in_range(len(det), min_period)
493	    if not usable:
494	        raise Halt("a profile of length %d carries no period of at least %d"
495	                   % (len(det), min_period))
496	    best_k, best_period = usable[0]
497	    best_power = power[best_k]
498	    for k, period in usable[1:]:
499	        if power[k] > best_power:
500	            best_k, best_period, best_power = k, period, power[k]
501	    spectrum = [{"cycles": k, "period": len(det) / k, "power": power[k],
502	                 "in_range": (len(det) / k) >= min_period - 1e-9}
503	                for k in sorted(power)]
504	    out = {
505	        "max_power": best_power,
506	        "wavelength": best_period,
507	        "cycles": best_k,
508	        "n_periods_in_range": len(usable),
509	        "profile_length": len(det),
510	        "spectrum": spectrum,
511	    }
512	    if keep_profile:
513	        out["profile"] = prof
514	        out["detrended"] = det
515	    return out

631	    """Largest period gap and largest ratio gap over cleared widths.
632	
633	    `cleared` is a list of (probe width, period in characters) pairs. Returns
634	    (None, None) when fewer than two widths cleared, so no pair exists.
635	    """
636	    if len(cleared) < 2:
637	        return None, None
638	    gap = 0.0
639	    ratio_gap = 0.0
640	    for i in range(len(cleared)):
641	        for j in range(i + 1, len(cleared)):
642	            a_w, a_l = cleared[i]
643	            b_w, b_l = cleared[j]
644	            gap = max(gap, abs(a_l - b_l))
645	            ratio_gap = max(ratio_gap, abs(a_l / float(a_w) - b_l / float(b_w)))

                   min_period: int = PERIOD_MIN, keep_profile: bool = False):
    """Largest power and its period, from one similarity matrix.

    Returns a dictionary. "max_power" is the largest power at any period from
    min_period up to the profile length. "wavelength" is that period, in the units of
    the matrix's own labels. When two periods tie on power, the longer one wins, so
    the answer never depends on ordering. The whole spectrum is returned every time,
    which is what the design requires to be saved for each shuffle draw.
    """
    prof = offdiag_profile(matrix, max_delta)
    det = poly_detrend(prof, degree)
    power = dft_power(det)
    usable = periods_in_range(len(det), min_period)
    if not usable:
        raise Halt("a profile of length %d carries no period of at least %d"
                   % (len(det), min_period))
    best_k, best_period = usable[0]
    best_power = power[best_k]
    for k, period in usable[1:]:
        if power[k] > best_power:
            best_k, best_period, best_power = k, period, power[k]
    spectrum = [{"cycles": k, "period": len(det) / k, "power": power[k],
                 "in_range": (len(det) / k) >= min_period - 1e-9}
                for k in sorted(power)]
    out = {
        "max_power": best_power,
        "wavelength": best_period,
        "cycles": best_k,
        "n_periods_in_range": len(usable),
        "profile_length": len(det),
        "spectrum": spectrum,
    }
    if keep_profile:
        out["profile"] = prof
        out["detrended"] = det
    return out


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Part 5. Endpoint arithmetic. Every function here is a pure function of numbers, so
# the self-test can plant values whose correct call is known in advance.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

RULE_SETUP = (
    "The text file's hash must equal the committed hash exactly, the layer count must "
    "equal 24, and the hidden size must equal 1024. Anything else is SETUP_FAILURE "
    "and halts the run before any measurement."
)
RULE_EXTRACT = (
    "All 48 documents at all 9 wrap widths must produce one forward pass each, 432 in "
    "total, with no variant flagged as reaching the context limit. Anything else is "
    "EXTRACT_INCOMPLETE and halts."
)
RULE_CALIBRATION = (
    "Every one of the three probe widths must yield a label window whose profile is "
    "long enough to detrend at degree 2 and to carry at least one period of 4 or "
    "more, under both labellings. Anything else is CALIBRATION_UNUSABLE and halts "
    "before any held-out number is computed."
)
RULE_ANCHOR = (
    "Held-out fit quality at width 140, at the best layer, must lie between 0.701 and "
    "0.861 inclusive. Outside that is ANCHOR_OUT_OF_BAND: an instrument fault that "
    "voids every wobble result of this run and blocks any next run. It is not "
    "evidence about the model."
)
RULE_CLEARED = (
    "The rank of the observed largest power among 200 label-shuffled draws, counting "
    "the observed value itself, must be 10 or better. That is the top 5 percent. "
    "Worse is NULL_NOT_CLEARED, meaning no separable wobble at that probe width."
)
RULE_COUNT = (
    "If no probe width clears its own shuffle draws, the reading depends on the "
    "measurable-range check. Wide counts measurable gives DECISIVE_NEGATIVE. Wide "
    "counts not represented gives RANGE_NOT_REPRESENTED. A range pattern matching "
    "neither reading gives NEGATIVE_NOT_CLASSIFIABLE."
)
RULE_WAVELENGTH_GAP = (
    "Over the probe widths that cleared their own shuffle draws, the largest gap "
    "between any two periods, in characters, must be at most 10. Larger rules out a "
    "single fixed period. Fewer than two widths clearing leaves the gap undefined."
)
RULE_RATIO_GAP = (
    "Over the probe widths that cleared their own shuffle draws, the largest gap "
    "between any two period-to-width ratios must be at most 0.1. Larger, together "
    "with a period gap above 10 characters, rules out a fixed proportion as well."
)
RULE_RANGE = (
    "At width 280, held-out fit quality is measured inside each bin of 35 label "
    "values, against that bin's own spread. Any bin starting above label 150 that "
    "exceeds 0.3 means wide counts ARE measurable. Otherwise, if all four bins "
    "ending at or below 140 exceed 0.5 and all three bins starting above 150 fall "
    "below 0.3, wide counts are NOT represented. Any other pattern is "
    "RANGE_PATTERN_UNMATCHED. The bin from 141 to 175 is recorded and excluded."
)
RULE_CONFOUND = (
    "At a probe width, the character-count wobble is credited over token position "
    "when the two periods differ by more than 3 characters, or when exactly one of "
    "the two labellings clears its own shuffle draws. Otherwise the wobble is "
    "CONFOUNDED_WITH_TOKEN_POSITION at that width."
)
RULE_HEADLINE = (
    "A failed anchor voids everything. Otherwise, two or more clearing widths are "
    "classified as INVARIANT when all period gaps are at most 10 characters, else "
    "PROPORTIONAL when all period-to-width ratio gaps are at most 0.1, else MIXED. "
    "Exactly one clearing width is UNDETERMINED by design. None clearing defers to "
    "the measurable-range check."
)


def decide_setup(hash_ok: bool, n_layers, hidden_size) -> str:
    if hash_ok and exact_config_match(n_layers, hidden_size):
        return "SETUP_OK"
    return "SETUP_FAILURE"


def decide_anchor(r2) -> str:
    if r2 is None or r2 != r2:                        # absent, or not a number
        return "ANCHOR_OUT_OF_BAND"
    return "ANCHOR_IN_BAND" if ANCHOR_LO <= r2 <= ANCHOR_HI else "ANCHOR_OUT_OF_BAND"


def null_rank(observed, draws) -> int:
    """Place of the observed value among the draws plus itself, largest first."""
    return 1 + sum(1 for v in draws if v >= observed)


def decide_cleared(rank: int) -> str:
    return "NULL_CLEARED" if rank <= NULL_RANK_MAX else "NULL_NOT_CLEARED"


def decide_range(low_r2s, high_r2s) -> str:
    if any(r is None for r in list(low_r2s) + list(high_r2s)):
        return "RANGE_CHECK_INCOMPLETE"
    if any(r > RANGE_HIGH_CEIL for r in high_r2s):
        return "WIDE_COUNTS_MEASURABLE"
    if all(r > RANGE_LOW_FLOOR for r in low_r2s) and all(r < RANGE_HIGH_CEIL for r in high_r2s):
        return "WIDE_COUNTS_NOT_REPRESENTED"
    return "RANGE_PATTERN_UNMATCHED"


def decide_count(n_cleared: int, range_decision: str) -> str:
    if n_cleared > 0:
        return "AT_LEAST_ONE_CLEARED"
    if range_decision == "WIDE_COUNTS_MEASURABLE":
        return "DECISIVE_NEGATIVE"
    if range_decision == "WIDE_COUNTS_NOT_REPRESENTED":
        return "RANGE_NOT_REPRESENTED"
    return "NEGATIVE_NOT_CLASSIFIABLE"


def pairwise_gaps(cleared):
    """Largest period gap and largest ratio gap over cleared widths.

    `cleared` is a list of (probe width, period in characters) pairs. Returns
    (None, None) when fewer than two widths cleared, so no pair exists.
    """
    if len(cleared) < 2:
        return None, None
    gap = 0.0
    ratio_gap = 0.0
    for i in range(len(cleared)):
        for j in range(i + 1, len(cleared)):
            a_w, a_l = cleared[i]
            b_w, b_l = cleared[j]
            gap = max(gap, abs(a_l - b_l))
            ratio_gap = max(ratio_gap, abs(a_l / float(a_w) - b_l / float(b_w)))
    return gap, ratio_gap


def decide_wavelength_gap(gap) -> str:
    if gap is None:
        return "GAP_UNDEFINED_FEWER_THAN_TWO_CLEARED"
    return ("WAVELENGTH_GAP_WITHIN_10" if gap <= INVARIANCE_MAX_GAP_CHARS
            else "WAVELENGTH_GAP_EXCEEDS_10")


def decide_ratio_gap(gap) -> str:
    if gap is None:
        return "GAP_UNDEFINED_FEWER_THAN_TWO_CLEARED"
    return ("RATIO_GAP_WITHIN_0.1" if gap <= PROPORTION_MAX_RATIO_GAP
            else "RATIO_GAP_EXCEEDS_0.1")


def decide_invariance(cleared) -> str:
    """The headline fork over the probe widths that cleared their own draws.

    A single fixed period is checked first, because it is the stronger claim about
    the model and the design lists it first. Both rules can hold at once when the
    periods sit close together; that case is recorded alongside the call.
    """
    if not cleared:
        return "NO_WIDTH_CLEARED"
    if len(cleared) == 1:
        return "UNDETERMINED"
    gap, ratio_gap = pairwise_gaps(cleared)
    if gap <= INVARIANCE_MAX_GAP_CHARS:
        return "INVARIANT"
    if ratio_gap <= PROPORTION_MAX_RATIO_GAP:
        return "PROPORTIONAL"
    return "MIXED"


def decide_confound(wl_chars, wl_token_in_chars, char_cleared, token_cleared) -> str:
    if wl_token_in_chars is None or token_cleared is None:
        return "TOKEN_CONTROL_NOT_COMPUTABLE"
    if abs(wl_chars - wl_token_in_chars) > CONFOUND_MARGIN_CHARS:
        return "CHARACTER_COUNT_DISTINGUISHED"
    if bool(char_cleared) != bool(token_cleared):
        return "CHARACTER_COUNT_DISTINGUISHED"
    return "CONFOUNDED_WITH_TOKEN_POSITION"


def decide_headline(anchor_decision: str, cleared, range_decision: str) -> str:
    """One call for the whole run, from the calls already made."""
    if anchor_decision != "ANCHOR_IN_BAND":
        return "VOID_ANCHOR_FAILED"
    if not cleared:
        return decide_count(0, range_decision)
    return decide_invariance(cleared)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Part 6. Ridge fitting from running totals.
#
# Storing every internal vector of every position would need over 40 gigabytes. It is
# not needed. A ridge fit and a fit-quality score depend on the data only through five
# running totals per layer: the sum of outer products of the vectors, the sum of the
# vectors, the sum of vector times label, the sum of labels, and the sum of squared
# labels. So the first stage accumulates those, per layer, per group of documents.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def wobble_with_null(x, labels, docs, window_lo, n_slots, max_delta, n_draws, rng,
                     spectra_path, unit):
    """Observed largest power and its shuffle draws, on one set of positions.

    Every draw's whole spectrum is written to `spectra_path`, one line per draw, as
    the design requires. The observed spectrum is the first line.
    """
    import numpy as np
    slots = slots_array(labels, window_lo, n_slots)
    mat, counts = means_by_slot(x, slots, n_slots)
    grand = mat.mean(axis=0, keepdims=True)
    centred = mat - grand
    cos = cosine_matrix(centred)
    observed = max_power_stat(cos, max_delta, keep_profile=True)
    dim, share = ambient_dimension(centred)

    with open(spectra_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        fh.write(json.dumps({
            "kind": "observed", "draw": None, "unit": unit,
            "profile_length": observed["profile_length"],
            "max_power": observed["max_power"], "wavelength": observed["wavelength"],
            "cycles": observed["cycles"],
            "spectrum": observed["spectrum"]}) + "\n")
        draws = []
        for i in range(n_draws):
            shuffled = shuffle_within_docs(labels, docs, rng)
            s2 = slots_array(shuffled, window_lo, n_slots)
            m2, _ = means_by_slot(x, s2, n_slots)
            c2 = m2 - m2.mean(axis=0, keepdims=True)
            stat = max_power_stat(cosine_matrix(c2), max_delta)
            draws.append(stat["max_power"])
            fh.write(json.dumps({
                "kind": "shuffle", "draw": i, "unit": unit,
                "profile_length": stat["profile_length"],
                "max_power": stat["max_power"], "wavelength": stat["wavelength"],
                "cycles": stat["cycles"],
                "spectrum": stat["spectrum"]}) + "\n")
    rank = null_rank(observed["max_power"], draws)
    return {"observed": observed, "draws": draws, "rank": rank,
            "counts": [int(c) for c in counts], "means": mat, "grand_mean": grand[0],
            "cosine": cos, "ambient_dimension": dim, "variance_share": share}


def stage_endpoints(args):
    import numpy as np

    prov = load_provenance()
    out_dir, work_dir = paths_for(args.results_dir)
    stim = stimulus_path(args.stimulus)
    design = design_record_path(args.design_record)
    gate = gate_record_path()
    calib_path = Path(out_dir) / "calibration.json"
    if not calib_path.exists():
        raise Halt("no calibration record at %s; the calibrate stage must run first"
                   % calib_path)
    with open(calib_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        calib = json.load(fh)
    if calib.get("decision") != "CALIBRATION_OK":
        raise Halt("the calibration record says %r, so no held-out number may be computed"
                   % calib.get("decision"))
    cv = calib["values"]
    alpha = float(cv["ridge_strength"])
    per_ap = {int(k): v for k, v in cv["per_aperture"].items()}

    tot = load_totals(work_dir)
    n_read = tot["n_read"]

    # ---- The layer sweep, and the anchor gate at width 140. -----------------
    # The record carries rounded numbers for reading. The best readout and the anchor
    # call are taken from the unrounded ones, so no rounding can move a decision.
    per_layer = []
    exact = []
    for layer in range(n_read):
        g, v, c, ls, lq, n = sum_groups(tot, TRAIN_GROUPS, layer)
        w, off = ridge_fit_from_stats(g, v, c, ls, n, alpha)
        row = {"readout": layer}
        ge, ve, ce, lse, lqe, ne = sum_groups(tot, TEST_GROUPS, layer)
        pooled, _, _ = r2_from_stats(w, off, ge, ve, ce, lse, lqe, ne)
        row["held_out_quality_pooled"] = round(float(pooled), 6)
        by_width = {}
        for width in WIDTHS:
            gw, vw, cw, lsw, lqw, nw = sum_groups(tot, ["test_w%d" % width], layer)
            r2w, _, _ = r2_from_stats(w, off, gw, vw, cw, lsw, lqw, nw)
            by_width[width] = float(r2w)
            row["held_out_quality_w%d" % width] = round(float(r2w), 6)
        per_layer.append(row)
        exact.append({"readout": layer, "pooled": float(pooled), "by_width": by_width})
    best_exact = max(exact, key=lambda r: r["pooled"])
    best_layer = int(best_exact["readout"])
    anchor_r2 = best_exact["by_width"][140]
    best = per_layer[best_layer]
    anchor_decision = decide_anchor(anchor_r2)
    print("[endpoints] best readout %d, pooled held-out quality %.6f, width-140 quality "
          "%.6f -> %s" % (best_layer, best_exact["pooled"], anchor_r2, anchor_decision))
    write_record(
        prov, out_dir, base_cell("endpoints", "anchor_gate", endpoint=1),
        inputs=record_inputs(prov, stim, design, gate,
                             extra=[(Path(work_dir) / "totals.npz", n_read)]),
        metric="Held-out fit quality at width 140, at the best readout, on text the earlier run never saw.",
        values={"best_readout": best_layer,
                "held_out_quality_w140": round(anchor_r2, 6),
                "held_out_quality_pooled": best["held_out_quality_pooled"],
                "ridge_strength": alpha,
                "ridge_argmax_interior_on_grid": cv["ridge_argmax_interior_on_grid"],
                "training_positions": int(sum(tot["n_pos"][k] for k in TRAIN_GROUPS)),
                "held_out_positions": int(sum(tot["n_pos"][k] for k in TEST_GROUPS)),
                "earlier_run_quality": PRIOR_ANCHOR,
                "earlier_run_readout": PRIOR_LAYER},
        threshold={"low": ANCHOR_LO, "high": ANCHOR_HI},
        decision_rule=RULE_ANCHOR,
        decision=anchor_decision,
        rows=per_layer,
        notes=("The best readout is chosen by held-out quality pooled over all nine wrap "
               "widths, exactly as the design says. The anchor number is that readout's "
               "quality at width 140 alone. The readout's location is recorded and never "
               "judged. The earlier value 0.780903 at readout 6 came from a different, "
               "disjoint text file on the same instrument lineage. " + RERUN_NOTE),
    )

    # ---- The wobble at each probe width, against its own shuffle draws. -----
    results = {}
    for a in APERTURES:
        info = per_ap[a]
        window_lo = int(info["character_window_low"])
        n_labels = int(info["n_labels"])
        max_delta = int(info["max_delta"])
        z = np.load(labels_file(work_dir, a), allow_pickle=False)
        test_mask = z["is_test"] == 1
        n_rows = int(test_mask.sum())
        x = read_aperture_layer(work_dir, a, best_layer, n_rows)
        docs_test = z["doc"][test_mask]
        char_test = z["char_label"][test_mask]
        token_test = z["token_label"][test_mask]

        spectra = Path(out_dir) / ("null_spectra_aperture-%d_labels-characters.jsonl" % a)
        rng = np.random.default_rng([SEED, a, 0])
        t0 = time.time()
        res = wobble_with_null(x, char_test, docs_test, window_lo, n_labels, max_delta,
                              N_DRAWS, rng, spectra, "characters")
        decision = decide_cleared(res["rank"])
        print("[endpoints] width %d: largest power %.6g at period %.2f characters, rank "
              "%d of %d -> %s (%.1f s)"
              % (a, res["observed"]["max_power"], res["observed"]["wavelength"],
                 res["rank"], N_DRAWS, decision, time.time() - t0))

        np.savez(Path(out_dir) / ("mean_vectors_aperture-%d_labels-characters.npz" % a),
                 labels=np.arange(window_lo, a + 1, dtype=np.int32),
                 counts=np.array(res["counts"], dtype=np.int32),
                 means=res["means"], grand_mean=res["grand_mean"],
                 cosine=np.array(res["cosine"], dtype=np.float64),
                 readout=np.array([best_layer]), aperture=np.array([a]))

        write_record(
            prov, out_dir,
            base_cell("endpoints", "wobble_vs_shuffle", endpoint=2, aperture=a),
            inputs=record_inputs(prov, stim, design, gate,
                                 extra=[(labels_file(work_dir, a), n_rows),
                                        (spectra, N_DRAWS + 1)]),
            metric="Rank of the observed largest power among 200 label-shuffled draws, at one probe width.",
            values={"aperture": a, "readout": best_layer,
                    "max_power": res["observed"]["max_power"],
                    "wavelength_chars": res["observed"]["wavelength"],
                    "cycles": res["observed"]["cycles"],
                    "profile_length": res["observed"]["profile_length"],
                    "n_periods_in_range": res["observed"]["n_periods_in_range"],
                    "rank": res["rank"], "draws": N_DRAWS,
                    "empirical_share": round(res["rank"] / (N_DRAWS + 1.0), 5),
                    "null_max": max(res["draws"]),
                    "null_median": sorted(res["draws"])[len(res["draws"]) // 2],
                    "character_window_low": window_lo, "character_window_high": a,
                    "n_labels": n_labels,
                    "held_out_rows": n_rows,
                    "positions_per_label_min": min(res["counts"]),
                    "positions_per_label_max": max(res["counts"]),
                    "ambient_dimension_at_95_percent": res["ambient_dimension"],
                    "variance_share_first_ten": [round(s, 6) for s in res["variance_share"][:10]],
                    "profile": [round(v, 8) for v in res["observed"]["profile"]],
                    "spectrum": res["observed"]["spectrum"],
                    "spectra_file": spectra.name,
                    "mean_vectors_file": ("mean_vectors_aperture-%d_labels-characters.npz" % a)},
            threshold={"rank_at_most": NULL_RANK_MAX, "draws": N_DRAWS},
            decision_rule=RULE_CLEARED,
            decision=decision,
            rows=[{"draw": i, "max_power": v} for i, v in enumerate(res["draws"])],
            notes=("Shuffling permutes the character-count labels inside each held-out "
                   "document, so every label keeps exactly the same number of positions. "
                   "With 200 draws the finest share this can resolve is about 0.5 percent. "
                   "The number of directions carrying 95 percent of the spread is recorded "
                   "here and constrains nothing, unlike the earlier run. Every draw's whole "
                   "spectrum is in the named file beside this record. " + RERUN_NOTE),
        )
        results[a] = {"char": res, "char_decision": decision,
                      "x": x, "docs": docs_test, "token": token_test,
                      "char_labels": char_test, "n_rows": n_rows}

    # ---- The token-position control, one record per probe width. ------------
    variants_path = Path(out_dir) / "rows_variants.jsonl"
    if not variants_path.exists():
        raise Halt("no per-variant rows at %s; the extract stage must run first"
                   % variants_path)
    chars_by_width = {a: 0 for a in APERTURES}
    with open(variants_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        for line in fh:
            row = json.loads(line)
            if row["split"] == "test" and row["width"] in chars_by_width:
                chars_by_width[row["width"]] += row["n_chars"]

    for a in APERTURES:
        info = per_ap[a]
        res = results[a]
        obs_wl = res["char"]["observed"]["wavelength"]
        char_cleared = res["char_decision"] == "NULL_CLEARED"
        token_hi = int(info["token_window_high"])
        tok_max_delta = int(info["token_max_delta"])
        n_rows = res["n_rows"]
        chars_per_token = chars_by_width[a] / float(n_rows) if n_rows else None
        vals = {"aperture": a, "readout": best_layer,
                "token_window_high": token_hi,
                "token_max_delta": tok_max_delta,
                "held_out_characters": chars_by_width[a],
                "held_out_positions": n_rows,
                "chars_per_token": (round(chars_per_token, 4) if chars_per_token else None),
                "character_wavelength_chars": obs_wl,
                "character_cleared_shuffle": char_cleared}
        note = ["The characters-per-token rate is measured on this probe width's own "
                "held-out documents, as the gate file's answer 5 requires, because the "
                "tokenisation shifts a little with the wrap width."]
        tok_wl_chars = None

        try:
            if not chars_per_token:
                raise Halt("no held-out positions at this probe width")

            rng = np.random.default_rng([SEED, a, 1])

            tres = wobble_with_null(res["x"], res["token"], res["docs"], 1, token_hi,

This question re-runs seed D2's aperture-invariance test with three instrument corrections, after seed D2 voided itself at its own anchor gate (records/seedD2_design_diff_triage.json; results_seedD2/out/, headline VOID_ANCHOR_FAILED; TAKEAWAYS_seedD2.md). Contamination is declared: the author has seen the voided outputs. Each correction below is derivable from artifacts that existed before seed D2 ran, and is marked with its derivation; the sealed predictions file re-registers expectations with that exposure stated.

Background, unchanged from seed D2: the original study (Gurnee et al., "When Models Manipulate Manifolds", Transformer Circuits, Oct 2025; Claude 3.5 Haiku) found a residual-stream curve tracking characters since the last newline, with faint off-diagonal similarity bands ("ringing") explained as Gibbs-style truncation. Seed D1 (records/seedD_v2_design_diff_triage.json, results_seedD/out/) measured on Pythia-410m-deduped step143000: held-out R-squared 0.781 at layer 6, layer selected and scored POOLED OVER WIDTHS 20 THROUGH 140; ambient dimension 1; no ripple at the one testable period. With ambient dimension 1 the theory's predicted spacing equals any probe window, so the decidable question is invariance across windows.

Question, unchanged: at this checkpoint (EleutherAI/pythia-410m-deduped, revision step143000, base model, no interventions - one cell; sweep, other models, causal tests out of scope), when the similarity structure of the character-count representation is measured at probe windows of 140, 200, and 280 characters, and a periodicity clears its shuffle null at any window, is its wavelength INVARIANT in characters across windows, or PROPORTIONAL to the window? No window clearing is a decisive negative up to 280 characters, subject to the represented-range check. The downloaded config is authoritative; 24 layers and hidden size 1024 are MEMORY (arXiv 2304.01373); mismatch halts. Layer index 0 is the embedding output; the best layer's location is recorded, never gated.

Stimuli, unchanged: stimulus_linewrap_v2.json (sha256 b0aa4255b5038d6fbc2e7314decf1011a5b5a13990098142e16ab44c6bba41dd), 48 documents, nine widths, documents 0-35 train and 36-47 test, text disjoint from seed D1's. Load exactly; halt if absent.

Definitions, with the corrections marked:

1. Labels, unchanged from seed D2 definition 1.

2. CORRECTED anchor and layer selection. The best layer is chosen by held-out R-squared pooled over widths 20 through 140 only - the same seven widths and the same pooling seed D1's committed runner used for both selection and scoring (derivation: construct identity, provable from run_seedD.py, which never saw widths 200 or 280). The anchor gate is that same pooled-over-seven-widths quality at that layer: it must lie between 0.701 and 0.861 (0.781 plus or minus 0.08, GUESS band for fresh text). Failing voids every wobble result and blocks any next seed. The width-140-only quality, and the width-200 and width-280 qualities, are recorded per layer, never gated (seed D2's error was gating a width-140-only number, at a layer dragged by the 200 and 280 legs, against this pooled reference).

3. Ridge readout, unchanged: grid {1, 10, 100, 1000, 10000, 100000}, five-fold cross-validation on train documents only, interior-argmax flag recorded.

4. Ripple statistic, per window in {140, 200, 280}, AT THE ANCHOR LAYER of definition 2, on test documents of that width: per-label mean vectors, grand mean subtracted, cosine matrix, off-diagonal profile, degree-2 polynomial detrend, discrete Fourier transform, statistic = maximum power over all whole-cycle periods from 4 characters up to the profile length. COMMITTED HERE (was a runner guess in seed D2): the profile length is the label count minus 20, so 120, 180, and 260. Ambient dimension recorded per window, constrains nothing.

5. Null, unchanged: 200 within-document label shuffles per window per labelling, same maximum statistic; clearing = observed exceeds all but the top 5 percent (rank 10 or better of 200); every draw's full spectrum saved; per-label mean vectors saved into fetched results. NEW, from the post-phase finding that seed D2's per-window records read clean in isolation: every per-window wobble and control record must carry the anchor gate's decision in its own values, so no record can be cited without its void status attached.

6. Invariance rule, unchanged: among clearing windows, all pairwise wavelength gaps at most 10 characters (GUESS) is INVARIANT; all wavelength-to-window ratios within 0.1 (GUESS) is PROPORTIONAL; neither is MIXED; exactly one clearing is UNDETERMINED; the headline is this fork.

7. CORRECTED represented-range check, at the anchor layer, width 280 test documents: within each of eight 35-label bins, the PEARSON CORRELATION between the global fit's prediction and the true label (derivation of the correction: within-bin R-squared of a global fit is bounded by one minus the squared ratio of global residual spread to bin spread; seed D1's recorded 0.78 implies a residual spread near 19 characters against a bin spread near 10, so the old construct was provably unable to reach its own thresholds - arithmetic available before seed D2 ran). Reading: wide counts are measurable if any bin starting above 175 has correlation at least 0.5 (GUESS); not represented if every bin at or below 140 reaches at least 0.5 and every bin above 175 stays below 0.2 (GUESS); otherwise unmatched. The 141-175 bin is recorded and excluded. A null wobble at windows 200 and 280 under "not represented" is RANGE_NOT_REPRESENTED, not evidence against the ripple.

8. Token-position control, unchanged from seed D2 (per-window characters-per-token, committed in records/GATE_COMMIT_seedD2.md answer 5; margin 3 characters; shortest period 4 in each labelling's own units). Both labellings' ranks and wavelengths recorded regardless of the character result - seed D2's (voided) diagnostics showed the token labelling clearing at rank 1 to 2 everywhere at its layer, and whether that positional periodicity persists at the anchor layer is itself worth recording.

Out of scope, unchanged, plus: no re-litigation of seed D2's voided numbers; they remain void.

The program state after three executed runs: the **curve** is now among the better-replicated small results around — 0.781031 vs 0.780903 on fully disjoint text, same layer, twice. The **ripple** is negative at 410m in the strongest sense available: at the aperture where the count is well represented, with every period searchable and no band censorship, the observed structure is *smoother than 199 of 200 shuffles*. The wide apertures died of representation collapse (a finding about training pressure, booked, not a ripple verdict).

Next after post returns: takeaways review, then seed D3 — the pre-registered scale fork. Sketch (to be pressure-tested against the post findings before authoring): cheapest cell on the ladder that can still carry the equilibrium-versus-fossil program later, which means Pythia-1.4b-deduped step143000 (checkpoints exist for a future sweep; Gemma-2-9B has t-tech's anchor but no released checkpoints, so it dead-ends the formation question). Headline endpoint shifts from "is there a ripple" to the **precondition**: does the count representation's ambient dimension reach the regime (~4+, vs Haiku's 6 and 410m's 1–3) where the Gibbs account predicts a resolvable ripple at all. One known wart to fix in the D3 seed: the token-control decision name reads "CHARACTER_COUNT_DISTINGUISHED" even when neither labeling cleared — noise distinguished from noise; the label needs a no-signal branch.

Pythia-1.4b is chosen over externally-anchored alternatives (Gemma-2-9B, reproduction R-squared 0.868) because only Pythia releases the 154 training checkpoints and exact data order the program's parent question (equilibrium versus fossil) requires; a ripple found here can be swept, one found in Gemma cannot.

Substrate facts: 24 layers and hidden size 2048 are MEMORY (Pythia paper, arXiv 2304.01373, table 1); the downloaded config is authoritative and a mismatch halts. Seed D2.1's width-280 bins showed fine resolution collapsing early even inside the fitted range (0.648 then 0.219, 0.153, 0.271); whether the same collapse holds at width 140 bears on whether a fine-scale ripple was ever measurable, and no run has recorded it.

Floor passes and no window clears with ambient dimension still below 4 everywhere - PRECONDITION_ABSENT_AT_1P4B, the expected continuation of the 410m result. Floor passes and ambient reaches 4 or more anywhere while no window clears - PRECONDITION_WITHOUT_RIPPLE, a strike against the capacity-truncation account itself. Any window clears - the invariance fork of seed D2.1 (INVARIANT / PROPORTIONAL / MIXED / UNDETERMINED) decides, and INVARIANT reopens the checkpoint sweep on THIS model, where checkpoints exist.

scope limitation, stated in the seed itself ("weaker than 410m's replication
anchor"). The compensating instrument is the pre-registered range check,
whose readings decide whether wide-window nulls count as evidence at all.

Sealed D3 scores booked — the bet lost, and honestly: the rung was supposed to extend the negative and instead returned a genuine puzzle. Post-phase cold read running on the D3 records now.

The decision the post will inform (UNDETERMINED has no pre-registered owner — this is the one place the chain leaves the next step open): the strongest candidate is a **targeted replication rung, D3.1** — third disjoint text slice, same model, one pre-registered hypothesis (does width-280 clear again, at the full-aperture period), plus the cheap discriminator the artifact hypothesis begs for: the same statistic at **layer 0**. Pythia's layer 0 is pure token embeddings under rotary — no computed count code, but all the column-locked lexical statistics (line-initial word starts, wrap-point effects). If the k=1 clearing shows at layer 0 too, it's text structure, not representation; if only at the anchor layer, the long-period component is real and the ladder conversation changes. Authoring waits for the elicit's questions.

# Does a Small Language Model's Character Counter Ripple? A Five-Run Chain.

Written 2026-08-22 by the orchestrating session, from the committed records
only. Every number below lives in a result record under results_seedD*/out/ or
a committed file in records/; nothing is restated from memory.

## The question, and where it came from

A study of a large closed model (Claude 3.5 Haiku) found that a language model
internally tracks how many characters have passed since the last line break,
as a smooth curve in its hidden activity, and that the curve's similarity
structure shows a faint repeating wave, a "ripple", explained as the cost of
squeezing a rich structure into about six usable directions. Nobody had
measured that ripple on an open model. This chain asked: does it exist in
open models whose full training history is public, where a later study could
watch it form?

Five runs executed, on rented single-graphics-card machines, total compute
cost about 3.60 dollars: two on Pythia-410m-deduped and three on
Pythia-1.4b-deduped, all at each model's final public training checkpoint,
using committed, hash-pinned text stimuli, three mutually disjoint text
samples, and pre-registered thresholds throughout.

## What was found

1. THE COUNTER IS REAL AND REPLICATES ALMOST EXACTLY. A linear reading of the
   character count from hidden activity, fit on training documents and scored
   on held-out ones (pooled over line widths 20 to 140), reached 0.780903 and
   then 0.781031 on the 410-million-weight model across two disjoint texts, a
   gap of 0.000128, both at layer 6 of 24. The 1.4-billion-weight model
   reached 0.876302 and then 0.879879 on two further disjoint texts, both at
   layer 5. Scale improves the counter.

2. THE COUNTER'S FINE RESOLUTION ENDS NEAR 70 CHARACTERS. Within stretches of
   35 count values, the correlation between predicted and true count on
   held-out text reads 0.646, 0.820, 0.211, 0.227 across counts 1 to 140 in
   one run, and 0.650, 0.830, 0.198, 0.244 in the next, on different text.
   Exact counting collapses past roughly 70 characters, which is where the
   training corpus's dominant hard-wrapped line length sits (about 70 to 72
   characters). Past that boundary the model knows roughly how far along the
   line it is, not exactly. On 280-character lines, counts above 175
   correlate at only 0.10 to 0.31: long lines are out-of-distribution
   wholesale.

3. NO RIPPLE, ANYWHERE TESTED. Under the final committed statistic (the
   strongest repeating component with at least two full cycles, judged
   against 200 label-shuffled comparison runs per case), no probe window (140,
   200, or 280 characters) cleared its null on either model, in either the
   character-count or the token-position labelling. At most windows the real
   structure is SMOOTHER than nearly every shuffled version (ranks up to 201
   of 200), which is what a clean low-dimensional curve with nothing folded
   into it looks like. The original study's ripple account did not transfer
   to these models at these scales.

4. THE ONE RECURRING "SIGNAL" IS THE CURVE ITSELF. A one-cycle, monotone
   component (falling about 0.36 to -0.16 across the widest window,
   correlation with position -0.92 to -0.998) beat the shuffle null twice at
   the widest window. It is not a repeating pattern: it is the counter's own
   smooth similarity decay, incompletely removed by the trend-removal step.
   The chain's one statistic change (barring the one-cycle bin) separates the
   established curve from the question asked on top of it.

5. THE RIPPLE'S PRECONDITION IS ABSENT. The count structure occupies 1 to 3
   directions at 95 percent of its spread in nearly every measurement; the
   original study's ripple lived at about 6. The single contrary reading
   (15 directions, one run, one window) collapsed to 2 on fresh text and
   varied tenfold with the percentage convention: it was measurement noise,
   exposed by pre-registered alternate conventions.

## What this means for the parent question

The parent program asked whether the ripple's geometry is an equilibrium or a
fossil, to be decided by sweeping Pythia's 154 public training checkpoints.
That sweep has no object at these scales: there is no ripple to track at
410m or 1.4b. The counter itself, and its 70-character resolution boundary,
ARE sweepable objects, and the boundary's location (at the training corpus's
wrap pressure) is itself a formation question. The transfer question (the
ripple exists in a far larger model; the largest anchored open model,
Gemma-2-9B, reproduction quality 0.868, releases no training checkpoints)
remains open and is a human decision.

## The instrument's own history, kept honest

The chain corrected itself five times, each correction committed before the
run that used it: a first run whose search band censored the predicted
periods (caught by registered-prediction verification against the source
paper); a second run voided by its own anchor gate after the anchor was built
from a mismatched construct (caught by the gate, diagnosed from the records);
a corrected rerun that replicated the anchor to four decimal places; a
scale rung whose only positive was a trend artifact in a single spectral bin
(caught by an independent reader re-deriving the winning shape from the
committed record); and a closing rung with that bin barred, which returned
the committed null. One run in five produced its intended headline on the
first try. Every failure became a named, committed correction; nothing was
re-scored after the fact; voided numbers stayed void.

## Where everything lives

Seeds in seeds/; committed designs, gate answers, deviations, and
registered-prediction files in records/; per-run results with self-describing
provenance records in results_seedD*/out/ (every shuffle draw's full
spectrum, every per-count average vector, every raw position row); sealed
predictions with scored outcomes in SEALED_PREDICTIONS.md; per-run reader
reports in TAKEAWAYS_seed*.md; budget in records/BUDGET.md (about 3.60
dollars of a 100-dollar cap).

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Density gate: coined project codes per 1000 words of prose.

A code is a token a first-time reader cannot parse: project-minted all-caps
labels and stage references. The whitelist holds ordinary all-caps English
and field-standard acronyms. Threshold from the retro's rerun-B result:
readable text sat under 10 codes per 1000 words; anchored text sat at 40+.

Exit 0 under threshold, 1 over. --selftest is model-free.
"""
import re, sys

WHITELIST = {"A","I","OK","NO","YES","AND","OR","NOT","THE","TO","IN","ON",
             "GPU","API","JSON","CI","PDF","URL","CPU","RAM","II","III","IV",
             "TODO","NB","PS","QA","AUROC","LLM","MATS","FAQ","BST","UTC"}
CODE = re.compile(r"\b[A-Z][A-Z0-9_\-]{2,}\b")
STAGE = re.compile(r"\bstage[- ]?\d+\b", re.I)
THRESHOLD = 10.0

def density(text):
    words = len(text.split())
    if not words:
        return 0.0, 0, 0
    codes = [t for t in CODE.findall(text) if t not in WHITELIST]
    n = len(codes) + len(STAGE.findall(text))
    return 1000.0 * n / words, n, words

def main():
    if "--selftest" in sys.argv:
        good = ("The model answers seven on every row while the underlying "
                "distribution moves under self-attributed failure. ") * 30
        bad = ("The SITREF REF drops under SELFQ but not OTHERM; PADM "
               "convicts the pad; stage-25 stands as committed. ") * 30
        dg, _, _ = density(good)
        db, _, _ = density(bad)
        assert dg <= THRESHOLD < db, (dg, db)
        print(f"selftest ok: {dg:.1f} (pass) vs {db:.1f} (fail)")
        return 0
    d, n, w = density(open(sys.argv[1]).read())
    print(f"{sys.argv[1]}: {d:.1f} codes/1000 words ({n} codes, {w} words); threshold {THRESHOLD}")
    return 0 if d <= THRESHOLD else 1

if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Scope gate: a sentence carrying a measured number must name its checkpoint
(which model or variant) or carry a footnote marker.

Retro evidence: a compression pass silently dropped "on the base checkpoint"
from the ranked list that answered the paper's title question. This gate
makes that deletion loud. Heuristic v1; extend MARKERS per host project.

Exit 0 clean, 1 with violations. --selftest is model-free.
"""
import re, sys

MARKERS = re.compile(
    r"\b(base|instruct|-it\b|9b|2b|27b|qwen|gemma|both checkpoints|both models)\b"
    r"|\^\d+|\[\^?\d+\]", re.I)
NUM = re.compile(r"[+\-]?\d+\.\d+|\d+%|\bCI\b|±|E\[")

def violations(text):
    sents = re.split(r"(?<=[.!?])\s+", text)
    return [s.strip() for s in sents if NUM.search(s) and not MARKERS.search(s)]

def main():
    if "--selftest" in sys.argv:
        ok = "The instruct model drops by 0.93 under self-attributed failure."
        bad = "The rating drops by 0.93 under self-attributed failure."
        assert not violations(ok) and violations(bad)
        print("selftest ok")
        return 0
    v = violations(open(sys.argv[1]).read())
    for s in v[:20]:
        print("UNSCOPED:", s[:120])
    print(f"{len(v)} unscoped result sentence(s)")
    return 1 if v else 0

if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
