# Does a Small Language Model's Character Counter Ripple? A Five-Run Chain.

Written by the orchestrating session on 2026-08-22, from the committed records
only. Every number below lives in a result record inside the per-run output
folders or a committed file in the records folder; nothing is restated from
memory. Scope markers: [1] means the base 410-million-weight model at its
final public training checkpoint; [2] means the base 1.4-billion-weight model
at its final public training checkpoint; [3] means the chain as a whole.

## The question, and where it came from

A study of a large closed model found that a language model internally tracks
how many characters have passed since the last line break, as a smooth curve
in its hidden activity, and that the curve's similarity structure shows a
faint repeating wave, a "ripple", explained as the cost of squeezing a rich
structure into about six usable directions. Nobody had measured that ripple
on an open model. This chain asked: does it exist in open models whose full
training history is public, where a later study could watch it form?

Five runs executed on rented single-graphics-card machines, total compute
cost about 3.60 dollars [3]: two runs on the base 410-million-weight model
and three on the base 1.4-billion-weight model, all at final public training
checkpoints, using committed, hash-pinned text stimuli, three mutually
disjoint text samples, and thresholds registered before each run.

## What was found

1. The counter is real and replicates almost exactly. A linear reading of the
   character count from hidden activity, fit on training documents and scored
   on held-out ones (pooled over line widths 20 to 140), reached 0.780903 and
   then 0.781031 on two disjoint texts, a gap of 0.000128, both at layer 6 of
   24 [1]. The larger model reached 0.876302 and then 0.879879 on two further
   disjoint texts, both at layer 5 [2]. Scale improves the counter.

2. The counter's fine resolution ends near seventy characters. Within
   stretches of 35 count values, the correlation between predicted and true
   count on held-out text reads 0.646, 0.820, 0.211, 0.227 across counts 1 to
   140 in one run, and 0.650, 0.830, 0.198, 0.244 in the next, on different
   text [2]. Exact counting collapses past roughly seventy characters, which
   is where the training corpus's dominant hard-wrapped line length sits
   (about 70 to 72 characters). Past that boundary the model knows roughly
   how far along the line it is, not exactly. On 280-character lines, counts
   above 175 correlate at only 0.10 to 0.31 [2]: long lines are
   out-of-distribution wholesale.

3. No ripple, anywhere tested. Under the final committed statistic (the
   strongest repeating component with at least two full cycles, judged
   against 200 label-shuffled comparison runs per case), no probe window
   (140, 200, or 280 characters) cleared its comparison on either base model,
   in either the character-count or the token-position labelling [3]. At most
   windows the real structure is smoother than nearly every shuffled version
   (ranks up to 201 of 200) [3], which is what a clean low-dimensional curve
   with nothing folded into it looks like. The original study's ripple
   account did not transfer to these models at these scales.

4. The one recurring "signal" is the curve itself. A one-cycle, falling
   component (dropping about 0.36 to minus 0.16 across the widest window,
   correlation with position minus 0.92 to minus 0.998) beat the shuffle
   comparison twice at the widest window [2]. It is not a repeating pattern:
   it is the counter's own smooth similarity decay, incompletely removed by
   the trend-removal step. The chain's one statistic change (barring the
   one-cycle bin) separates the established curve from the question asked on
   top of it.

5. The ripple's precondition is absent. The count structure occupies one to
   three directions at 95 percent of its spread in nearly every measurement
   on both base models [3]; the original study's ripple lived at about six.
   The single contrary reading (15 directions, one run, one window) collapsed
   to 2 on fresh text and varied tenfold with the percentage convention [2]:
   it was measurement noise, exposed by the registered alternate conventions.

## What this means for the parent question

The parent program asked whether the ripple's geometry is an equilibrium or a
fossil, to be decided by sweeping the smaller model family's 154 public
training checkpoints. That sweep has no object at the scales tested here:
there is no ripple to track on either base model [3]. The counter itself, and
its seventy-character resolution boundary, are sweepable objects, and the
boundary's location (at the training corpus's wrap pressure) is itself a
formation question. The transfer question stays open: the ripple exists in a
far larger closed model, and the strongest-curved anchored open model (a
nine-billion-weight model, reproduction quality 0.868 on its base form)
releases no training checkpoints. Both forks are a human decision.

## The instrument's own history, kept honest

The chain corrected itself five times, each correction committed before the
run that used it [3]. A first run's search band censored the predicted
periods (caught by registered-prediction verification against the source
paper). A second run voided itself at its own anchor gate after the anchor
was built from a mismatched construct (caught by the gate, diagnosed from
the records). A corrected rerun replicated the anchor to four decimal places
on the base model [1]. A scale rung's only positive was a trend artifact in a
single spectral bin (caught by an independent reader re-deriving the winning
shape from the committed record) [2]. A closing rung with that bin barred
returned the committed null [2]. One run in five produced its intended
headline on the first try [3]. Every failure became a named, committed
correction; nothing was re-scored after the fact; voided numbers stayed void.

## Where everything lives

Seed questions sit in the seeds folder. Committed designs, gate answers,
deviations, and registered-prediction files sit in the records folder.
Per-run results sit in the per-run output folders, as self-describing
records that carry their own inputs, rules, and calls, alongside every
shuffle draw's full spectrum, every per-count average vector, and every raw
position row. The sealed predictions ledger at the repository root carries
every prediction and its scored outcome. Each run also has its own reader
report at the repository root, and the budget ledger sits in the records
folder (about 3.60 dollars spent of a 100-dollar cap, across both base
models) [3].

# Does a Small Language Model's Character Counter Ripple? A Five-Run Chain.

Written 2026-08-22 by the orchestrating session, from the committed records
only. Every number below lives in a result record under results_seedD*/out/ or
a committed file in records/; nothing is restated from memory.

## The question, and where it came from

A study of a large closed model (Claude 3.5 Haiku) found that a language model
internally tracks how many characters have passed since the last line break,
as a smooth curve in its hidden activity, and that the curve's similarity
structure shows a faint repeating wave, a "ripple", explained as the cost of
squeezing a rich structure into about six usable directions. Nobody had
measured that ripple on an open model. This chain asked: does it exist in
open models whose full training history is public, where a later study could
watch it form?

Five runs executed, on rented single-graphics-card machines, total compute
cost about 3.60 dollars: two on Pythia-410m-deduped and three on
Pythia-1.4b-deduped, all at each model's final public training checkpoint,
using committed, hash-pinned text stimuli, three mutually disjoint text
samples, and pre-registered thresholds throughout.

## What was found

1. THE COUNTER IS REAL AND REPLICATES ALMOST EXACTLY. A linear reading of the
   character count from hidden activity, fit on training documents and scored
   on held-out ones (pooled over line widths 20 to 140), reached 0.780903 and
   then 0.781031 on the 410-million-weight model across two disjoint texts, a
   gap of 0.000128, both at layer 6 of 24. The 1.4-billion-weight model
   reached 0.876302 and then 0.879879 on two further disjoint texts, both at
   layer 5. Scale improves the counter.

2. THE COUNTER'S FINE RESOLUTION ENDS NEAR 70 CHARACTERS. Within stretches of
   35 count values, the correlation between predicted and true count on
   held-out text reads 0.646, 0.820, 0.211, 0.227 across counts 1 to 140 in
   one run, and 0.650, 0.830, 0.198, 0.244 in the next, on different text.
   Exact counting collapses past roughly 70 characters, which is where the
   training corpus's dominant hard-wrapped line length sits (about 70 to 72
   characters). Past that boundary the model knows roughly how far along the
   line it is, not exactly. On 280-character lines, counts above 175
   correlate at only 0.10 to 0.31: long lines are out-of-distribution
   wholesale.

3. NO RIPPLE, ANYWHERE TESTED. Under the final committed statistic (the
   strongest repeating component with at least two full cycles, judged
   against 200 label-shuffled comparison runs per case), no probe window (140,
   200, or 280 characters) cleared its null on either model, in either the
   character-count or the token-position labelling. At most windows the real
   structure is SMOOTHER than nearly every shuffled version (ranks up to 201
   of 200), which is what a clean low-dimensional curve with nothing folded
   into it looks like. The original study's ripple account did not transfer
   to these models at these scales.

4. THE ONE RECURRING "SIGNAL" IS THE CURVE ITSELF. A one-cycle, monotone
   component (falling about 0.36 to -0.16 across the widest window,
   correlation with position -0.92 to -0.998) beat the shuffle null twice at
   the widest window. It is not a repeating pattern: it is the counter's own
   smooth similarity decay, incompletely removed by the trend-removal step.
   The chain's one statistic change (barring the one-cycle bin) separates the
   established curve from the question asked on top of it.

5. THE RIPPLE'S PRECONDITION IS ABSENT. The count structure occupies 1 to 3
   directions at 95 percent of its spread in nearly every measurement; the
   original study's ripple lived at about 6. The single contrary reading
   (15 directions, one run, one window) collapsed to 2 on fresh text and
   varied tenfold with the percentage convention: it was measurement noise,
   exposed by pre-registered alternate conventions.

## What this means for the parent question

The parent program asked whether the ripple's geometry is an equilibrium or a
fossil, to be decided by sweeping Pythia's 154 public training checkpoints.
That sweep has no object at these scales: there is no ripple to track at
410m or 1.4b. The counter itself, and its 70-character resolution boundary,
ARE sweepable objects, and the boundary's location (at the training corpus's
wrap pressure) is itself a formation question. The transfer question (the
ripple exists in a far larger model; the largest anchored open model,
Gemma-2-9B, reproduction quality 0.868, releases no training checkpoints)
remains open and is a human decision.

## The instrument's own history, kept honest

The chain corrected itself five times, each correction committed before the
run that used it: a first run whose search band censored the predicted
periods (caught by registered-prediction verification against the source
paper); a second run voided by its own anchor gate after the anchor was built
from a mismatched construct (caught by the gate, diagnosed from the records);
a corrected rerun that replicated the anchor to four decimal places; a
scale rung whose only positive was a trend artifact in a single spectral bin
(caught by an independent reader re-deriving the winning shape from the
committed record); and a closing rung with that bin barred, which returned
the committed null. One run in five produced its intended headline on the
first try. Every failure became a named, committed correction; nothing was
re-scored after the fact; voided numbers stayed void.

## Where everything lives

Seeds in seeds/; committed designs, gate answers, deviations, and
registered-prediction files in records/; per-run results with self-describing
provenance records in results_seedD*/out/ (every shuffle draw's full
spectrum, every per-count average vector, every raw position row); sealed
predictions with scored outcomes in SEALED_PREDICTIONS.md; per-run reader
reports in TAKEAWAYS_seed*.md; budget in records/BUDGET.md (about 3.60
dollars of a 100-dollar cap).

## The experiment, complete

Five executed runs, three disjoint text samples, two models, **$3.60 of the $100 cap**. Committed close: **NO_REPEATING_PATTERN_UP_TO_280** — the counting-manifold ripple does not transfer to Pythia at 410m or 1.4b. Synthesis delivered above (`CHAIN_TAKEAWAYS.md`, both language gates pass at 0.0 codes and 0 unscoped sentences).

**The three findings that survive everything:**
1. **The counter replicates almost eerily** — 0.780903 / 0.781031 at 410m (disjoint texts, gap 0.000128, layer 6 both times); 0.876302 / 0.879879 at 1.4b (layer 5 both times). Scale improves it.
2. **Its fine resolution ends at ~70 characters** — bin correlations 0.65/0.82 then 0.20/0.24, replicated across disjoint texts to two decimals — exactly the Pile's hard-wrap pressure. The model counts precisely inside its training distribution's line length and only coarsely beyond. This is the chain's genuinely new, sweepable object.
3. **No ripple, and the theory's precondition is absent** — ambient dimension 1–3 everywhere stable (the one "15" collapsed to 2 on fresh text), observed structure *smoother* than the shuffle nulls, and the only recurring above-null component identified as the curve's own monotone decay leaking through the detrend — the established finding re-detected, not a hidden wave.

**The final elicit's last challenge, answered on the record:** the barred one-cycle component ranks 1/201 again on fresh text with a near-identical shape — which is precisely what "it's the curve itself" predicts, and what "it's a hidden ripple" cannot explain (position-correlation −0.92 to −0.998 is monotone, not oscillatory). Two bookkeeping catches booked (token-max population ambiguity; design prose overstating one check's authority).

**The meta-experiment's ledger** — one run in five produced its intended headline first try; every other failure surfaced as a halt, a void, or a named committed correction, and none survived into a claim: the band censorship (caught by register-then-verify), the anchor construct mismatch (caught by the gate), the trend-bin artifact (caught by an independent reader), the writer's omitted gate block (caught and attributed). Sealed predictions: every one scored, misses kept.

**Two forks now await your decision**, deliberately unowned by any seed: sweep the *counter and its 70-char boundary* across the 154 checkpoints (the formation question survives even though the ripple died), or run the Gemma-2-9B transfer cell (anchored at 0.868, but no checkpoints — a dead end for formation). Everything needed for either is committed in the repo.

content.text:
## The research question

The parent question, from the proposal: **is a structure a model learns an equilibrium or a fossil** — does its geometry keep responding to the model's current constraints, or does it record the conditions of its formation? To ask that, you need a structure to track. The chosen one was the **ripple**: the original paper found models encode "characters since the last newline" as a smooth internal curve, and that this curve's similarity structure carries a faint repeating wave, explained as the cost of squeezing a rich structure into ~6 usable dimensions. The chain's operational question became: **does that ripple exist at all in open models whose training history is public?** — because only there could formation ever be watched.

## The hypothesis

Stated, from the paper's own §2.5: the ripple is what **optimal capacity-rationing** looks like — a model that must represent ~150 distinguishable count values in a handful of dimensions truncates the structure like a cut-off Fourier series, and the truncation leaves visible waves. Implied by that mechanism, and made testable by us: the ripple should appear wherever the counter appears, with a wavelength set by the model's code rather than by our measuring window, and it needs room to exist — several dimensions, not one.

## What the experiments tried to find

Five runs, each one decidable question. First: does the counter replicate at all on an open model (a gate — a published number to hit before anything else counts). Then: is there any repeating component in the counter's similarity structure that beats 200 label-shuffled versions of the same data — measured at three window sizes (140, 200, 280 characters), so that a real wave would keep its wavelength in characters while a measurement artifact would stretch with the window. Alongside: does the counter even represent counts that large; does the pattern follow characters or tokens; and does the counter's code occupy enough dimensions for the truncation story to apply. Each run's thresholds and refuting outcomes were written down before it ran.

## What we observed

Four things, each in a committed record:

1. **The counter is real and unusually replicable.** 0.7809 then 0.7810 on disjoint texts at the 410M model, same layer; 0.876 then 0.880 at 1.4B. Scale strengthens it.
2. **Its precision ends at ~70 characters** — replicated to two decimals across texts. That is the training corpus's dominant hard-wrapped line length. The model counts exactly where its data made counting matter, and only roughly beyond.
3. **No ripple.** No window, no model, no labelling produced a repeating component above chance. Mostly the real structure was *smoother* than the shuffles — what a clean one-dimensional curve with nothing folded into it looks like. And the precondition is absent: the counter lives in 1–3 dimensions, not the ~6 where the paper's mechanism operates.
4. **The one recurring above-chance signal was the counter itself** — a monotone similarity decay leaking through the trend-removal step, twice mistakable for a finding until its shape was read: it falls, it never repeats.

So the answer to the operational question is no — the ripple does not transfer to these open models, most plausibly because their counters are too low-dimensional for the truncation mechanism to produce waves. The parent question stands, but its object changed: at these scales there is no ripple whose formation could be watched. What *can* now be watched forming is the counter and its 70-character precision boundary — a structure that visibly carries the imprint of its training pressure, which is the fossil question in its simplest possible form.

## Optimal capacity-rationing

The model has to represent about 150 different count values, and it wants two things at once. It wants nearby counts to be *distinguishable* — "column 67" and "column 68" must point in usefully different directions, or the model can't decide where to break a line. And it has almost no room — the residual stream is shared with everything else the model tracks, so the counter is rationed to a handful of directions. With 150 dimensions to spend, both wants are trivially satisfied: give every count its own direction, done — the paper notes the desired similarity structure is *trivially realizable* at full dimension. Rationed to ~6, the best available move is to keep only the largest-scale components of that ideal structure and drop the fine ones — exactly like truncating a Fourier series. The dropped terms don't vanish politely; their absence shows up as overshoot waves around what remains. That is the Gibbs phenomenon, and the paper's claim ("rippled manifolds optimally trade off capacity constraints… with maintaining the distinguishability of different scalar values") is that the ripple isn't a defect — it's what the *optimal* compromise necessarily looks like. Their appendix simulation shows the waves arise even when the solution is found dynamically, not just in the closed-form ideal.

Our null is consistent with the mechanism rather than against it: Pythia's counter occupies 1–3 directions, not ~6. A model keeping only one mode isn't rationing among many — there's nothing to truncate, so the theory itself predicts no visible ripple. We confirmed the precondition's absence, not the mechanism.

## Posing a formation question about the counter

This is, pleasingly, the proposal's own pre-registered fallback — its go/no-go section says: if the ripple dies, degrade to *"when does the count manifold form, and does its dimensionality expand or contract."* The chain has now earned that question and equipped it. Posed in the house style, a seed D4 would fix:

- **The axis:** Pythia's 154 public checkpoints — the substrate was chosen for exactly this, and `batch_viewer.py` gives the cumulative hard-wrapped-token exposure before each step, the data-side timeline only Pythia permits.
- **The objects:** the two twice-replicated endpoint properties — pooled curve quality, and the four-bin precision profile whose collapse marks the boundary.
- **The fork:** equilibrium versus fossil, recast. *When* does the counter form (which checkpoint does quality rise)? Does the boundary appear *with* the counter or sharpen afterward? And once formed, does the boundary drift as training continues and the residual stream crowds (equilibrium), or lock and hold (fossil)? Exposure correlation gives the third leg: does formation timing track cumulative wrapped-text seen?
- **The anchor and gate:** our final-checkpoint numbers *are* the anchor cell — the sweep's last point must reproduce 0.781 and the bin profile with the already-thrice-validated instrument. One-cell gate before fan-out: step 0 (random init) as the negative control the chain never ran, plus one mid-training checkpoint.
- **Cost:** the instrument is light (~2 minutes of measurement per checkpoint); 154 checkpoints is roughly $10–15, well inside the cap.

## How the boundary differs from the published findings, with citations

Both published results report the counter as a *single global property*. Gurnee et al. ("When Models Manipulate Manifolds," Transformer Circuits, Oct 2025; arXiv 2601.04480) report Claude 3.5 Haiku tracking counts crisply across their full stimulus range (up to ~150 characters; probe R² 0.985), with no precision boundary inside it — but Haiku's training data is closed, so nothing about pressure could be checked, and they hedge that the crispness may reflect having *chosen* a task the model does well. Sinii & Balagansky ("Chasing the Counting Manifold in Open LLMs," huggingface.co/spaces/t-tech/manifolds, Feb 2026) report one pooled number per model (Pythia-410m: 0.724) — no resolution along the count axis, no ripple test.

Our bin construct — within-35-label correlation between prediction and truth — is new to this chain, and it localizes the precision. What it found: at the 1.4b base model, precision holds through counts 1–70 (0.65, 0.82–0.83) and collapses beyond (0.20–0.24), replicated on disjoint texts to two decimals. Seventy characters is where the Pile's dominant hard-wrapped pressure sits — Gutenberg at 2.17% of the mix, wrapped at ~70–72 characters; Enron at ~72 (the Pile, arXiv 2101.00027; PG-19; percentages from the proposal's verified table). So the difference is threefold: it's a *profile*, not a scalar; it shows the open-model counter is *range-limited*, not merely weaker; and because Pythia's corpus is public, the boundary's alignment with training pressure is checkable rather than speculative — which is what makes it a formation object.

## The evidence, honestly inventoried

**Strong:** counter replication — four independent runs, two models, three hash-pinned mutually disjoint text samples, agreement to 0.000128 at 410m; every number in a self-describing record with input hashes and pre-written decision rules. No-ripple — six primary shuffle-null tests (two models × three windows) plus the first run's banded test, all with full per-draw spectra saved and re-derivable; the final rung pre-registered and clean. Precondition absence — ambient dimension recorded at three conventions per window per run; the single outlier (15) fell to 2 on fresh text.

**Good but narrower than the summary sentence suggests:** the 70-character boundary rests on the *1.4b* width-140 bin pair. The 410m runs measured bins only on 280-character lines (out-of-distribution, where precision collapsed even earlier, after ~35); the 410m *in-distribution* profile was never recorded, because the bin diagnostic was only added at the third rung. A D4 must close that gap.

**Correlational only:** boundary-at-pressure is an alignment of two numbers, not an intervention. The causal version (train on differently-wrapped corpora) exists in the proposal's tier list, unrun.

**Known limits, all booked:** one text source (three slices of one novel — style homogeneity in every does_not_test), base models only, two scales, final checkpoints only, no step-0 control yet.

content.text:
## What D4 tests, simply

Every run so far looked at finished models. D4 looks at the same model *while it was being built*. The counter and its precision boundary exist at the end of training; D4 asks: **when did they appear, and once present, did they ever move?** If the structure snaps into place early and then holds its shape — same quality, same boundary, same few dimensions — through a hundred thousand further training steps, it behaves like a fossil: a record of the conditions that made it, carried unchanged. If instead its properties keep drifting as the model's internal space fills with everything else it learns, it behaves like an equilibrium: continuously re-negotiated. This is the parent question of the whole program, finally asked of an object we have actually proven exists.

## The hypothesis

Stated: **the counter is a fossil of training pressure.** It forms early — hard-wrapped text is common, the skill is cheap (a 19-million-weight Pile model already has "predict newlines in width-limited text" as a discrete skill, per the quantization-of-skills work cited in the proposal) — its precision boundary sits at the corpus's ~70-character wrap length from the first moment it is measurable, and counter, boundary, and dimensionality then hold still for the rest of training. The rival: formation is gradual or late, and the properties drift measurably after formation.

## How the experiment is built on it

Everything is inherited and thrice-validated; only the axis is new. One model (the base 410-million-weight one — cheapest, and anchored twice on this exact instrument), one committed stimulus (the same file whose final-checkpoint anchor we already hold: 0.781031, layer 6), and **twelve named public checkpoints**, log-spaced from initialization to the end (step 0, 512, 1k, 2k, 4k, 8k, 16k, 32k, 64k, 96k, 128k, 143k). Per checkpoint: curve quality per layer, the four-bin precision profile at the best layer, dimension counts recorded at three conventions, best-layer location recorded. The ripple legs are dropped — there is no ripple to track, by the chain's own committed close. Three structural economies: the gate cell is the *final* checkpoint, which must reproduce our own 0.781031 before any earlier checkpoint counts (and it measures the one gap in the evidence — the 410m in-distribution bin profile — either way); step 0 is the never-run negative control (random initialization should read near zero); and because Pythia's corpus is *pre-shuffled*, hard-wrapped exposure grows linearly with steps, so formation timing in steps *is* formation timing in exposure — no corpus download needed. Twelve cells fit one box under the 90-minute cap, roughly a dollar and a half.

## Prediction, and what I anticipate observing

Sealed before any agent runs: the final checkpoint reproduces its anchor and shows the boundary in-distribution (~0.7 confident); quality crosses half its final value **early**, between steps 2k and 16k — the first few percent of training; the boundary appears *together with* the counter, not as a later sharpening (my most uncertain call, near a coin flip, and the most interesting cell either way); after formation, quality, boundary, and dimension **hold** inside committed bands to the end (~0.65); the best layer may wander in the formation window and then fix; dimension stays at 1–3 throughout — no transient high-dimensional phase (if this one misses, it would be the most valuable miss of the chain, echoing the transient-structure literature).

## What would be sufficient evidence, and of what

Sufficient for the **fossil reading**: a bounded formation window (quality rise and boundary appearance located between two adjacent grid points), followed by every later checkpoint holding inside the pre-registered bands (boundary ratio range ≤ 0.15, quality range ≤ 0.1) across the remaining ~90% of training. Sufficient for the **equilibrium reading**: committed drift beyond those bands, monotone in steps, after formation. And the honest ceiling on what either would prove: this is evidence of *when the structure formed and whether it subsequently moved* — nothing more. It cannot say *why* it formed then (correlational; the causal corpus-manipulation test is a different, unrun tier), cannot resolve dynamics finer than the grid, and cannot speak to seed-dependence (that needs the PolyPythias runs, out of scope). On a pre-shuffled corpus, "fossil" specifically means *formed early under a stationary mixture, then static* — the sharpest version distinguishable from equilibrium here, since the mixture itself never changes.

Proceeding: seed, seal, design.

The chain's twice-replicated objects are the substrate here: on the base 410-million-weight model, held-out counting quality 0.780903 and 0.781031 on disjoint texts, both at layer 6 (records/seedD_v2_design_diff_triage.json, records/seedD2_1_design_diff_triage.json); on the base 1.4-billion-weight model, a four-bin precision profile whose fine resolution ends near 70 characters (0.646/0.820/0.211/0.227, then 0.650/0.830/0.198/0.244 on fresh text), matching the training corpus's dominant hard-wrap length of about 70-72 characters (counting_manifold_formation_proposal.md, verified table). One known evidence gap, closed by this rung's gate cell: the 410m in-distribution bin profile was never measured.

Question: when, during training, did the counter and its precision boundary form, and once formed, did they move? At twelve named public checkpoints of EleutherAI/pythia-410m-deduped - HuggingFace revisions step0, step512, step1000, step2000, step4000, step8000, step16000, step32000, step64000, step96000, step128000, step143000 (MEMORY: the release provides step0, powers of two to 512, then every 1000; arXiv 2304.01373) - measure per checkpoint, with the committed instrument: (a) held-out counting quality per layer, pooled over wrap widths 20-140; (b) the four-bin precision profile at the best layer, width 140 (within-35-label Pearson correlation between prediction and truth, bins 1-35, 36-70, 71-105, 106-140); (c) ambient dimension recorded at 90, 95, and 99 percent, never gated; (d) the best layer's location, recorded. No ripple legs: the chain's committed close found nothing to track, and this rung does not relitigate it.

The hypothesis under test, stated: the counter is a fossil of training pressure - it forms early, its boundary sits at the corpus wrap length from first measurability, and counter, boundary, and dimension then hold still. The rival: post-formation drift.

Substrate facts: base model, no interventions; 24 layers and hidden size 1024 are MEMORY (arXiv 2304.01373, table 1), config-mismatch halts; layer index 0 is the embedding output. Exposure note, load-bearing: the training corpus is served PRE-SHUFFLED (proposal, verified), so the hard-wrapped fraction per batch is stationary and cumulative exposure is linear in step count - formation timing in steps is formation timing in exposure, and no corpus download is needed or permitted here.

Stimuli: stimulus_linewrap_v2.json (sha256 b0aa4255b5038d6fbc2e7314decf1011a5b5a13990098142e16ab44c6bba41dd), unchanged - the same committed file behind the 0.781031 anchor, 48 documents at nine widths, documents 0-35 train and 36-47 test. Load exactly; halt if absent. Same labels, ridge grid {1, 10, 100, 1000, 10000, 100000}, five-fold train-only cross-validation per checkpoint, one base seed 0, provenance records with per-record gate flags - all as in the committed instrument lineage (records/GATE_COMMIT_seedD3_1.md binds anything unnamed).

Definitions, fixed here:

1. Gate cell, run first: the final checkpoint (step143000) must reproduce its own anchor - held-out quality pooled over widths 20-140 within 0.02 of 0.781031 (GUESS band; same text, same instrument, same model - tighter than any fresh-text band). Failing voids the sweep as an instrument fault. Its bin profile also closes the known 410m gap, whatever it shows.

2. Boundary ratio, per checkpoint: the mean of bins one and two minus the mean of bins three and four. The boundary is PRESENT when the ratio is at least 0.3 (GUESS, from the 1.4b values where it reads about 0.5). If the ratio is below 0.3 at the final checkpoint, the boundary-trajectory readings below are recorded as NOT_PRESENT_AT_FINAL, the quality-trajectory readings still stand, and the boundary questions transfer to a future 1.4b sweep - pre-registered, not a failure.

3. Formation step: the first checkpoint whose pooled quality reaches 0.5 (GUESS). Formed: the first checkpoint whose pooled quality reaches 90 percent of the final checkpoint's value.

4. Hold test, the fork's decider: across every checkpoint at or after "formed", the boundary ratio's range must stay within 0.15 and the pooled quality's range within 0.10 (both GUESS). Inside both bands: HELD. Outside either, with the drift monotone in steps: DRIFTED. Outside either, non-monotone: UNSTABLE_NOT_CLASSIFIABLE.

5. Step0 is the negative control: pooled quality at initialization is expected near zero; a step0 quality above 0.3 (GUESS) is an instrument alarm that voids the sweep (label leakage or a probe reading surface statistics).

Pre-registered readings: gate fails - VOID_ANCHOR_FAILED. Step0 alarm - VOID_CONTROL_FAILED. Otherwise: FORMED_EARLY_AND_HELD (formation step at or before step16000, hold test HELD - the fossil-consistent reading); FORMED_LATE_AND_HELD (formation after step16000, HELD); FORMED_AND_DRIFTED (either formation timing, hold test DRIFTED - the equilibrium-consistent reading); NOT_FORMED_BY_FINAL (final quality below 0.5 - contradicts two anchors, treated as instrument fault). Recorded alongside, never gated: whether the boundary appears at the formation step or sharpens later (the ratio at the formation step versus at "formed"); the best layer's trajectory; the dimension trajectory at three conventions.

Out of scope: why formation happens when it does (correlational only; the causal corpus-manipulation test is a different tier); dynamics finer than the twelve-point grid; seed-dependence (PolyPythias); the 1.4b sweep; any ripple question; any training-data download. Compute note for costing: twelve checkpoints of a 410-million-weight model, one measurement pass each, on one rented box under its 90-minute cap.

content.text:
## What fossil versus equilibrium really means

Take the counter's boundary at ~70 characters. Two stories produce that same final snapshot. **Equilibrium**: the structure is being held in place, continuously, by present forces — the model re-derives it, in effect, from its current situation: the data mixture it sees, and the crowding of everything else it must represent in the same shared space. Change the forces and the structure moves. **Fossil**: the structure was carved once, during a formation window, and then simply persisted — present forces no longer act on it; what you see records conditions that may no longer obtain. The two are indistinguishable in any single snapshot. They separate only in time: an equilibrium tracks its moving constraints; a fossil sits still while they move. One subtlety our substrate makes sharp: Pythia's corpus is pre-shuffled, so the *data* pressure never changes — the only constraint that moves during training is internal crowding, as the model learns everything else. So for D4, "HELD" specifically means *insensitive to crowding*, and "DRIFTED" means the structure keeps renegotiating its allocation as the space fills.

## What the source documents say about ramifications

The Anthropic paper says nothing — the errata is explicit: no training dynamics, no checkpoints, formation entirely absent; its §2.5 optimality argument is normative, and reading it as an *equilibrium claim* is the proposal's move, not the paper's. The proposal's ramification framing is the deeper one: the naive version of this question — "could training have gone otherwise?" — is largely settled and deflationary (runs become linearly mode-connected after 1.5–16% of training; curriculum effects on final internals fade by a billion weights). The live version is **endpoint insufficiency**: an endpoint can be *uniquely determined* by the data and still be *lossy about its own construction* — the transient-ridge result is a whole computational phase occupied and then erased, invisible at the end; circuit membership at formation versus at the end overlaps by only ~0.3. Against that, one striking positive: training-order can be read back from activations at ~90% and survives thirty epochs of shuffled retraining. So the field's picture: history is partly erased, partly readable, and nobody has systematically asked which structures fall on which side.

## What I would say

The ramifications sort by which answer wins, per structure. If structures are equilibria, a final model is *self-explanatory*: interpretability of the endpoint is physics — derive the structure from present constraints, and expect interventions (fine-tuning, continued training, capacity changes) to reshape it predictably. If structures are fossils, a final model is *natural history*: its internals record early training, which cuts two ways — you gain forensics (reading history, provenance, early-data effects out of weights) and you inherit inertia (early-formed representations that later training, including alignment training, may fail to move). My actual expectation is that the dichotomy resolves per-structure: cheap, pressure-matched skills — like a counter for the corpus's one dominant line length — fossilize early and hold; contested, capacity-squeezed structures keep renegotiating. The valuable output of a D4-style measurement isn't the label; it's learning *which regime a given structure lives in*, because that tells you whether to treat it as movable.

## Is there good evidence?

For the question being live: yes, and it's in the documents — Frankle's window is solid, the transient ridge is solid in its domain, the training-order-residue result is striking but single-lab, small-scale, fine-tuning-only. For *this object*: no evidence exists yet in either direction. Our boundary-at-pressure finding is consistent with the fossil story but proves nothing — a static snapshot cannot distinguish the stories, and under a stationary mixture even the equilibrium story predicts the boundary sits at the pressure. That is exactly the gap D4 is built to close, and the honest limit stands: twelve grid points can bound the formation window and test the hold, not explain either.

Continuing — checking the D4 design run.

Answers of record to the diff's four questions:

1. Both formation markers stay, because they answer different questions: the
   0.5 crossing locates when the counter becomes usable (formation step); the
   90-percent-of-final crossing starts the hold test (formed). One is about
   appearance, the other about stability.
2. The $2.50 estimate comes from twelve one-pass measurements of a small
   model on one box; the ledger (records/BUDGET.md, ~$3.6 spent of $100)
   governs, and the 90-minute box cap bounds the run physically.
3. Each checkpoint uses its own best layer, selected by its own pooled
   quality - the layer trajectory is itself a recorded observable (the seed
   predicts migration during formation). Fixing layer 6 everywhere would
   presume the answer.
4. Yes: the four-bin score is the within-bin Pearson correlation, exactly as
   the seed states it.

input.content:
This is the corrected formation rung, after seed D4 voided itself at its own negative control and both of its gate cells returned discoveries (records/seedD4_design_diff_triage.json; results_seedD4/out/). Contamination is declared: the author has seen those two measured cells. The corrections below derive from them, and the derivations are stated.

What seed D4's gates measured, both committed: (a) the anchor cell reproduced 0.781031 exactly on the base 410-million-weight model - and its boundary ratio at the final checkpoint is minus 0.091, so the 70-character fine-resolution boundary, twice replicated on the base 1.4-billion-weight model, is ABSENT at 410m: the boundary is scale-emergent, and the formation sweep must run where the object exists. (b) The initialization checkpoint decodes character position at pooled quality 0.345 - a randomly initialized network already carries partially decodable positional structure (rotary attention phases), with a measured signature: quality flat across all layers (about 0.34 from layer 2 to 24, best layer at the sweep edge), and inverted across widths (negative at narrow widths, minus 2.48 at width 20; positive only on long lines where count tracks absolute position). The formation baseline is therefore about 0.35, not zero, and my seed D4 alarm ceiling of 0.3 was a wrong guess about untrained networks - the control worked, and measured the right number.

Question: when, during training, did the base 1.4-billion-weight model's counter and its 70-character precision boundary form, and once formed, did they move? At twelve named public checkpoints of EleutherAI/pythia-1.4b-deduped - revisions step0, step512, step1000, step2000, step4000, step8000, step16000, step32000, step64000, step96000, step128000, step143000 (MEMORY: the suite shares one release scheme; arXiv 2304.01373) - measure per checkpoint with the committed instrument: held-out counting quality per layer pooled over wrap widths 20-140; the four-bin precision profile and boundary ratio at that checkpoint's own best layer, width 140; per-width quality and the per-layer profile shape (the two initialization signatures above), recorded; ambient dimension at three conventions, recorded; best layer and ridge strength with grid-edge degeneracy flags, per records/GATE_COMMIT_seedD4.md, binding here too.

Hypothesis, unchanged: fossil of training pressure - counter and boundary form early and then hold. Rival: post-formation drift.

Substrate facts: base model, no interventions; 24 layers and hidden size 2048 are MEMORY (arXiv 2304.01373, table 1), config-mismatch halts; layer index 0 is the embedding output; same tokenizer family as 410m. Pre-shuffled corpus: exposure is linear in steps; no data download.

Stimuli: stimulus_linewrap_v2.json (sha256 b0aa4255b5038d6fbc2e7314decf1011a5b5a13990098142e16ab44c6bba41dd) - the text behind BOTH final-checkpoint anchors for this model: pooled quality 0.876302 at layer 5, and width-140 bins 0.646/0.820/0.211/0.227, giving boundary ratio 0.514 (records/seedD3_design_diff_triage.json, results_seedD3/out/). Load exactly; halt if absent. Instrument lineage per records/GATE_COMMIT_seedD3_1.md binds anything unnamed.

Definitions, with the corrections marked:

1. Gate cell, run first: step143000 must reproduce pooled quality within 0.02 of 0.876302 AND show the boundary (ratio at least 0.3; its committed prior value on this text is 0.514). Either failing voids the sweep as an instrument fault.

2. CORRECTED control semantics (derived from seed D4's measured floor): step0 is a BASELINE measurement, not a near-zero alarm. Its pooled quality is recorded as the floor B; expected range 0.2 to 0.45 (GUESS, from 410m's measured 0.345). The only void alarm: B at or above 0.7 times the anchor quality (about 0.61) - the probe would then be reading most of its signal from untrained structure. The initialization signatures (flat-across-layers; negative-at-narrow-widths) are recorded at step0 and every checkpoint, never gated.

3. CORRECTED formation definitions, baseline-relative: formation step = the first checkpoint whose pooled quality reaches B plus 0.5 times (anchor minus B). Formed = the first checkpoint reaching B plus 0.9 times (anchor minus B). Boundary formation keeps its absolute bar: ratio at least 0.3 (the measured initialization baseline of the ratio is about minus 0.08, effectively zero, so no baseline correction is needed there).

4. Hold test, unchanged: across checkpoints at or after "formed", boundary-ratio range within 0.15 and pooled-quality range within 0.10 (GUESS bands): HELD. Outside either, monotone in steps: DRIFTED. Otherwise UNSTABLE_NOT_CLASSIFIABLE.

5. Recorded, never gated: whether the boundary ratio crosses 0.3 at, before, or after the quality formation step (does precision arrive with usability, or later); the best-layer trajectory (initialization is flat - the first checkpoint where a clear interior peak appears is the counter's localization moment, recorded as the first checkpoint whose best layer is interior AND whose peak exceeds the layer-median quality by at least 0.1, GUESS); the dimension trajectory.

Pre-registered readings: gate fails - VOID_ANCHOR_FAILED. Baseline alarm - VOID_CONTROL_FAILED. Otherwise: FORMED_EARLY_AND_HELD (formation step at or before step16000, hold HELD); FORMED_LATE_AND_HELD; FORMED_AND_DRIFTED; UNSTABLE_NOT_CLASSIFIABLE per definition 4; NOT_FORMED_BY_FINAL (contradicts two committed anchors; instrument fault). Boundary trajectory readings: BOUNDARY_WITH_COUNTER (ratio crosses 0.3 at or before the quality formation step), BOUNDARY_AFTER_COUNTER (crosses later), BOUNDARY_NOT_FORMED_BY_FINAL (contradicts the gate cell; instrument fault).

Out of scope: why formation happens when it does; dynamics finer than the twelve-point grid; seed-dependence; the 410m quality-only sweep (its boundary is absent, measured; a quality-only 410m sweep is a possible later rung); any ripple question; any data download. Compute note: twelve checkpoints of a 1.4-billion-weight model, one measurement pass each, one box, under its 90-minute cap.

# Model-free reachability control for seed D4.1's classification rules,
# run 2026-08-22 BEFORE the box, per the design triage's author queue.
# Rules exactly as committed: B-relative crossings, hold bands 0.10/0.15.
STEPS=[0,512,1000,2000,4000,8000,16000,32000,64000,96000,128000,143000]
ANCHOR=0.876
def classify(q, r):  # q,r: dicts step->quality/ratio (trained ckpts incl final)
    B=q[0]
    f_thr=B+0.5*(ANCHOR-B); formed_thr=B+0.9*(ANCHOR-B)
    trained=STEPS[1:]
    form=[s for s in trained if q[s]>=f_thr]
    formd=[s for s in trained if q[s]>=formed_thr]
    if not form: return "NOT_FORMED_BY_FINAL"
    if not formd: return "NOT_FORMED_BY_FINAL(90pc never)"
    f0,fd=form[0],formd[0]
    post=[s for s in trained if s>=fd]
    qr=max(q[s] for s in post)-min(q[s] for s in post)
    rr=max(r[s] for s in post)-min(r[s] for s in post)
    held = qr<=0.10 and rr<=0.15
    if held: lab="FORMED_EARLY_AND_HELD" if f0<=16000 else "FORMED_LATE_AND_HELD"
    else:
        qs=[q[s] for s in post]; mono=all(x<=y for x,y in zip(qs,qs[1:])) or all(x>=y for x,y in zip(qs,qs[1:]))
        rs=[r[s] for s in post]; monor=all(x<=y for x,y in zip(rs,rs[1:])) or all(x>=y for x,y in zip(rs,rs[1:]))
        lab="FORMED_AND_DRIFTED" if (mono or monor) else "UNSTABLE_NOT_CLASSIFIABLE"
    return lab+f" (form@{f0}, formed@{fd})"
import math
def sig(step,mid,width): return 1/(1+math.exp(-(math.log(step+1)-math.log(mid))/width))
cases={
 "early-sigmoid-flat": ({s:0.35+0.53*sig(s,2000,0.3) for s in STEPS}, {s:(0.5 if s>=2000 else -0.05) for s in STEPS}),
 "late-sigmoid-flat":  ({s:0.35+0.53*sig(s,48000,0.3) for s in STEPS}, {s:(0.5 if s>=64000 else -0.05) for s in STEPS}),
 "form-then-drift-up": ({s:min(0.88,0.35+0.53*sig(s,2000,0.3)+0.12*s/143000) for s in STEPS}, {s:(0.3+0.25*s/143000 if s>=2000 else -0.05) for s in STEPS}),
 "noisy-plateau":      ({s:0.35+0.53*sig(s,2000,0.3)+(0.09 if s in(32000,96000) else -0.03 if s in(16000,64000,128000) else 0) for s in STEPS}, {s:(0.5+(0.12 if s in(32000,96000) else -0.09 if s==64000 else 0) if s>=2000 else -0.05) for s in STEPS}),
 "never-forms":        ({s:0.35+0.05*sig(s,48000,0.5) for s in STEPS}, {s:-0.05 for s in STEPS}),
}
reached=set()
for name,(q,r) in cases.items():
    q[143000]=ANCHOR if name!="never-forms" else q[143000]
    lab=classify(q,r); reached.add(lab.split(" ")[0])
    print(f"{name:22s} -> {lab}")
need={"FORMED_EARLY_AND_HELD","FORMED_LATE_AND_HELD","FORMED_AND_DRIFTED","UNSTABLE_NOT_CLASSIFIABLE","NOT_FORMED_BY_FINAL"}
print("ALL FIVE LABELS REACHABLE:", need.issubset(reached))
EOF

import json, math
# Verify from raw saved rows at step143000: what statistic reproduces the recorded bins?
rows=[json.loads(l) for l in open('results_seedD4_1/out/rows_positions_w140_step143000.jsonl')]
import collections
def pearson(xs,ys):
    n=len(xs); mx=sum(xs)/n; my=sum(ys)/n
    cov=sum((x-mx)*(y-my) for x,y in zip(xs,ys))
    vx=sum((x-mx)**2 for x in xs); vy=sum((y-my)**2 for y in ys)
    return cov/math.sqrt(vx*vy) if vx>0 and vy>0 else float('nan')
def r2(pred,true):
    n=len(true); mt=sum(true)/n
    sse=sum((p-t)**2 for p,t in zip(pred,true)); sst=sum((t-mt)**2 for t in true)
    return 1-sse/sst if sst>0 else float('nan')
key_pred=[k for k in rows[0] if 'pred' in k][0]
key_true=[k for k in rows[0] if 'label' in k or 'true' in k][0]

content.text:
The arc is complete. Final report.

## The formation result, in full

**What was asked:** fossil or equilibrium — does the counter record its formation or track its present constraints? **What was measured:** neither story, and better than both. Four phases across twelve checkpoints of the 1.4b model, all gates passing exactly (anchor 0.876302 to the last digit; initialization baseline 0.341, scale-invariant against 410m's 0.345):

1. **Step 512** — a crude counter already at 94% of final quality, living deep (layer 23). The entire rise is inside the grid's first, unmeasured interval.
2. **Steps 2k–8k** — a destructive reorganization: quality regresses (0.851 → 0.715), fine precision falls *below its initialization value* (boundary ratio −0.248), the representation re-expands to ~100 directions. The transient build-then-teardown the formation literature predicts, measured on a named, twice-anchored object.
3. **Step 16k** — relocation: best layer jumps from 22 to 6.
4. **Steps 64k–143k** — consolidation: the precision boundary forms *last*, at 45% of training, then sits within 0.014; dimensionality keeps compressing 12 → 3 through the final checkpoint.

**Verdict per committed rules: UNSTABLE_NOT_CLASSIFIABLE** — correct and instructive: the "formed" milestone fired at step 512, before the teardown, and no committed rule assumed formation could regress. The recorded-only fields carry the resolution: from its own crossing, the boundary is fossil-still. So the answer is **per-property**: usability is instant; location and precision fossilize, but only after a mid-training demolition and rebuild; dimensionality behaves like an equilibrium still settling when training ends.

**The final cold read earned its pay twice:** it challenged the statistic labels, and re-derivation from raw rows settled both ways — the bin fields are genuine Pearson (recomputed 0.6460/0.8196/0.2106/0.2266 against recorded 0.646/0.820/0.211/0.227), while one record note misnamed the R² quality field. It also fixed four honesty items now booked: the boundary-stability label flips with the startpoint choice (both recorded), formation is bounded not timed, width-20 lines never work at any checkpoint (−0.888 at final) while pooling hides it, and six of seven widths aren't re-derivable from raw output.

**Ledger:** seven executed rungs (two self-voided, both informatively), ~**$8.30** of $100, every sealed prediction scored — the formation rung went 3 hits, 3 misses, 1 partial, and the misses are the science: the sealed "most valuable miss" (a transient high-dimensional phase) is exactly what fired. Synthesis delivered above with the formation chapter, both gates at zero. Project memory updated with the open forks — the finer grid inside 0–512 and 2k–16k, the two-phase-aware hold construct, seed-stability via the multi-seed release, the width-20 anomaly, and the Gemma transfer cell — all awaiting your pick.

content.text:
## The evidence for that claim — audited, and it doesn't fully hold

Graded against the chain's own rules (every recalled fact cites a source or gets marked), that sentence was an unmarked overreach, and you were right to press it. What the committed sources actually support is two *narrow* gap claims, both verified in the proposal document: first, *"no one has tracked a specific, theoretically-motivated task manifold across pretraining"* — supported there by the split it documents: final-model geometry characterized (the original paper; the reproduction), checkpoint geometry characterized only *in aggregate* (whole-model curves of collapse, expansion, consolidation); second, *"the retrospective inverse — given only the endpoint landscape, what can you infer about the sequence that produced it — is unposed."* Those are cited, specific, and were true as of the document's verification date.

What I cannot support is the universal I uttered. The same document lists work that *has* asked formation questions of specific structures: when attention circuits form, a specific transient structure building and dissolving, circuit membership at formation versus at the end (overlap ~0.3), training-order residue in activations. So formation-of-a-structure has been asked, several times. The defensible version of my sentence: the *classification program* — taking named structures and systematically sorting their properties into "locked at formation" versus "still tracking constraints," which is what our formation rung ended up doing for one structure — is not something the committed sources show anyone doing. Even that carries caveats I must own: my knowledge ends January 2026, the documents' verification is August 2026, I ran no literature sweep, and absence claims are exactly the kind the pipeline exists to catch. Mark it: the narrow gaps are SOURCED; the universal was MEMORY-grade and is retracted to the narrow form.

## The original research question

The parent question, from the proposal: **is a learned structure an equilibrium or a fossil** — does its geometry keep responding to the model's current constraints, or does it record the conditions of its formation and simply persist? To ask it, you need a specific structure whose formation you can watch, which is why the corpus had to be one with public training checkpoints. The chosen entry object was the **ripple** the original closed-model study found in the character-counting curve.

## The hypothesis

Stated, two layers deep. For the entry object: the ripple is what *optimal capacity-rationing* looks like — a model forced to represent ~150 count values in a handful of directions truncates the ideal structure like a cut-off Fourier series, and the truncation shows as waves; so the ripple should exist wherever the counter exists with enough dimensions. For the parent question, once the object changed: the counter is a *fossil of training pressure* — formed early, its precision boundary set at the corpus's dominant line length, then motionless.

## What the experiments tried to find

Seven pre-registered rungs, each one decidable question. First: does the counter replicate on open models (an anchor gate before anything counted). Then: does any repeating component beat two hundred label-shuffled controls, at three window sizes so a real wave would keep its wavelength while an artifact stretched with the window — twice, at two model scales, with the instrument corrected between rungs when its own gates caught faults. Then, the object having earned it: twelve checkpoints from initialization to the end, asking when counter and boundary appear, and whether anything moves afterward — gated on reproducing our own anchors and on measuring, rather than assuming, what an untrained network already decodes.

## What we observed

Five things, every number in a committed record. **The counter is real and severely replicable** — 0.781 twice at the smaller model on disjoint texts (agreeing to 0.0001), 0.876 twice at the larger. **The ripple does not exist here** — no window, no scale, no labelling beat chance; the real structure was usually *smoother* than its shuffles; and the precondition was absent: the counter lives in one to three directions, not the ~six the mechanism needs. **The precision boundary sits at the corpus's ~70-character wrap pressure and is scale-emergent** — present at 1.4 billion weights, absent at 410 million. **Untrained networks already decode position** at quality ~0.34, identically at both scales — the formation baseline is not zero. And **formation is four-phase**: a crude counter within 512 steps, a destructive mid-training reorganization where precision falls below its initialization value and the representation re-expands, relocation to an early layer, then consolidation in which the boundary forms *last* — at 45% of training — and thereafter never moves, while dimensionality keeps compressing to the final checkpoint. So the parent question's answer, for this structure, is **per-property**: usability is instant and permanent, location and precision fossilize only after a teardown-and-rebuild, and dimensionality is an equilibrium still settling when training stops.

content.text:
The latest rung — the twelve-checkpoint formation sweep on the 1.4-billion-weight model — told us four things, one per phase of a trajectory neither hypothesis predicted:

1. **The counter is learned almost instantly.** By step 512 — 0.4% of training — quality is already 94% of its final value. The whole climb from the untrained floor happens below the grid's first interval, so we bounded formation, we didn't time it. The floor itself was the rung's first surprise: an *untrained* network already decodes character position at 0.34, nearly identical at both model scales — attention's positional machinery gives the probe something to read before any learning occurs.

2. **The early counter gets partly torn down.** Between steps 2,000 and 8,000, quality regresses (0.85 → 0.72), fine precision falls *below its initialization value*, and the representation re-expands from ~37 directions back to ~100. A build-then-demolish transient — the shape the formation literature describes in toys, here measured on a named, twice-anchored structure in a real model.

3. **The structure then relocates and consolidates.** The best layer jumps from layer 22 to layer 6 around step 16,000, and the 70-character precision boundary — the thing we originally set out to track — forms *last of all*, crossing its bar only at step 64,000, forty-five percent of the way through training. After that it moves by 0.014, total, ever. Meanwhile dimensionality keeps compressing, twelve directions down to three, and is still shrinking at the final checkpoint.

4. **The committed verdict was "not classifiable," and that is itself the finding about our rules.** The hold test opened at the premature step-512 milestone, because no pre-registered rule imagined formation could *regress*. The recorded-only fields carry the resolution — measured from its own birth, the boundary is fossil-still — but the headline honestly reports that our formation constructs assumed monotone growth and the model refused.

Net: the fossil-versus-equilibrium question dissolved into a per-property answer. Usability: instant, permanent. Location and precision: fossils, but only after a mid-training teardown and rebuild. Dimensionality: an equilibrium that hadn't finished settling when training ended. And the practical lesson for the next seed, if there is one: the interesting intervals are the two the grid can't see into — steps 0–512, where the counter is born, and 2,000–16,000, where it is torn apart and rebuilt somewhere else.

content.text:
## What "the equilibrium hadn't finished settling" means

Concretely: the number of directions carrying 95% of the count representation's spread was still falling when the released checkpoints ran out — 21 at step 32k, 12 at 64k, 6 at 96k, 3 at both 128k and 143k, arriving at 3 only in the last stretch. Every other property had long since stopped moving: quality flat, boundary frozen since 64k, layer fixed. Dimensionality alone was still on a monotone trajectory at the end. The meaning: that property isn't a set-and-forgotten record of formation — it looks like an ongoing renegotiation, the model continuously re-compressing the counter's allocation as the shared representational space fills with everything else it learns. So the final checkpoint's "the counter uses three directions" is a snapshot of a process, not a settled fact — had training continued, the number had no visible reason to stop. Two honesty bounds: "dominant" matters (the 99%-variance tail stayed at 80–130 directions throughout — what compresses is the head, not the tail), and the count is convention-sensitive, which is why we recorded it at three cutoffs.

## How this contrasts with the primary paper

The paper (Gurnee et al., *When Models Manipulate Manifolds*) is a portrait of one finished model; our chain is the same object examined across scale and time. The contrasts, point by point:

- **Dimensionality:** they found the count structure occupying ~6 directions at 95% — enough room for truncation waves. Our models allocate 1–3. This doesn't contradict their §2.5 tradeoff; it resolves it differently — a smaller model buys less distinguishability, and below the ripple's precondition the same optimization predicts a smooth curve, which is what we measured.
- **The ripple:** present and central for them; absent everywhere for us, at every window, both scales, with the real structure smoother than chance. Their account didn't transfer — most plausibly because the precondition doesn't.
- **Layer:** they report probes crisp *after layer 1*; we find the counter at layers 5–6 of 24, agreeing with the open-model reproduction, whose authors explicitly flagged this as contradicting the original.
- **Crispness and its edge:** they saw crisp counting across their full range and no boundary. We found precision ending at ~70 characters — the corpus's dominant hard-wrap length — and found that boundary only at the larger model. They couldn't have seen ours: their training data is closed, so pressure and precision can't be aligned there even in principle.

## Did they comment on what we ended up finding?

Almost entirely no — and that's documented, not inferred. The verified errata is blunt: formation is *"not in the paper — no training dynamics, no checkpoints."* So the four-phase trajectory, the destructive mid-training reorganization, the boundary forming last and then fossilizing, the still-compressing dimensionality, the untrained network's 0.34 positional floor — none of it is predicted, contradicted, or discussed there. Three partial touches are the closest they come. First, their §2.5 optimality argument poses our question *statically*: it claims the geometry is an optimal allocation but never asks when the optimum is reached or whether it keeps moving — the fossil-versus-equilibrium fork was the proposal's construction on top of their snapshot, not theirs. Second, their appendix toy shows ripples *"arise even when the solution is found dynamically"* — their one formation-adjacent gesture, but it simulates the emergence of a structure our models never form. Third, their own hedge — *"the crispness of the representations… may be due to how well the model does the task"* — is, in retrospect, the qualitative shadow of our sharpest finding: crispness ends where training pressure ends. We measured the boundary their caveat gestured at, on a corpus open enough to check it against.

# Summary of Paper Measurements and Findings

**Quantities Measured Across Checkpoints:**
The paper measures "effective rank (RankMe) and eigenspectrum decay (α-ReQ)" across training phases to assess representation geometry.

**Models Studied:**
OLMo (1B-7B parameters) and Pythia (160M-12B parameters) during pretraining and post-training stages.

**Three Phases of Representation Geometry Evolution (in order):**
1. **Warmup phase**: Characterized by "rapid representational collapse"
2. **Entropy-seeking phase**: Features "manifold's dimensionality expands substantially, coinciding with peak n-gram memorization"
3. **Compression-seeking phase**: Involves "anisotropic consolidation, selectively preserving variance along dominant eigendirections"

**Scope of Analysis:**
The paper tracks aggregate whole-model geometry rather than specific named task representations. It examines how post-training methods (SFT, DPO, RLVR) further transform overall representation structure, with effects on "in-distribution performance" and "out-of-distribution robustness" broadly rather than measuring particular downstream tasks.

content.content:
# Paper Summary

## Measurements Across Training Checkpoints

The paper tracks **geometric measures and linear probes** across:
- **Models**: Six transformer sizes (405K–151M parameters) plus three Pythia language models (160M–2.8B)
- **Tasks**: Eight algorithmic tasks (144 task×level×model combinations)
- **Key metrics**: Representation dimensionality (rankme), linear probe performance, behavioral accuracy

## Headline Finding

The core claim: "representations first collapse to a low-dimensional state, then recover, and only then does behavioral performance improve." This establishes a **temporal dissociation between geometry and behavior**—geometric changes precede capability acquisition.

## Task Structure & Theory

The paper examines task-difficulty-dependent patterns. For hard tasks, it reports "a clear gap: geometry changes first, behavior follows" with a "precursor gap of ~49K training steps" on logical deduction in Pythia-2.8B. Easy tasks show simultaneous geometric and behavioral change with no detectable precursor.

The key theoretical insight: whether geometric precursors are observable depends on "task difficulty relative to model capacity." Linear probes reveal task-relevant information in hidden states *before* behavioral readiness, suggesting representations reorganize geometrically before being actionable.

content.text:
## "Their account transfers"

An *account* is an explanatory story, not just a result: here, the original paper's claim that the ripple exists because the model optimally rations dimensions — squeeze a rich similarity structure into ~6 directions and truncation waves appear. To *transfer* means the story keeps working when you move it to a new model. Precision matters about which layer failed to transfer: the **phenomenon** did not — no ripple, at any window, on either open model. The **deeper optimization story** was not refuted, because at the dimensionality our models actually allocate (1–3 directions), that same story predicts a smooth curve with no waves. What failed to transfer is the paper's *visible signature*; whether the underlying tradeoff theory is right is untested here, because at these scales it has nothing to predict waves about.

## The precondition

The ripple mechanism needs the model to keep *several* frequency components of the ideal similarity structure — think of a truncated Fourier series: keeping three or four terms of a series produces visible overshoot wiggles; keeping one term produces a smooth arc, nothing to wiggle. Dimensions convert to frequency components at roughly two directions per component. The original model spent ~6 directions ≈ 3 components → waves. Our models spend 1–3 directions ≈ one component → the theory itself predicts no resolvable ripple. That allocation — enough dimensions (~4 or more) for truncation to leave visible oscillation — is the precondition, and we measured it absent at both scales, with the one contrary reading (15 directions, once) collapsing to 2 on fresh text.

## The ripple, and its relation to the counting manifold

The counting manifold is the path the model's internal state traces as the count runs 1, 2, 3, … — one point per count value, forming a curve in activation space. Ideally the model wants nearby counts distinguishable *and* far-apart counts unconfused: similarity high only near the diagonal of the count-versus-count similarity matrix. That ideal needs about as many dimensions as there are counts. Rationed to ~6, the best compromise keeps only the broadest similarity components — and the discarded fine components don't vanish gracefully: the reconstruction oscillates around the ideal, so similarity between counts doesn't fall smoothly with distance but swings, producing faint bands parallel to the diagonal. That oscillation is the ripple. Geometrically it means the curve coils: far-apart counts periodically swing back into partial alignment, with the coil period as the wavelength. So the ripple is not an object beside the manifold — it is the visible *cost* of compressing the manifold, and the original paper's bridge sentence makes the same point from the feature side: ringing, in the manifold picture, is interference in the superposition picture.

## The nearest neighbors in the literature (checked, not recalled)

Two papers watch representations evolve across the same public checkpoints and are the closest kin, both verified today. One tracks effective rank and eigenspectrum decay across OLMo and Pythia pretraining and finds three aggregate phases — warmup collapse, an entropy-seeking expansion coinciding with peak memorization, then compression-seeking consolidation preserving dominant directions. Our counter's trajectory is the *per-structure* version of exactly that shape: expansion at steps 2k–8k, compression to the very end. The other runs linear probes and dimensionality across hundreds of Pythia checkpoints on eight algorithmic tasks and finds "geometry changes first, behavior follows," with collapse-then-recover preceding capability. That one is closest in machinery — probes over Pythia checkpoints — but task-aggregate. The toy-model transient-structure work (a structure built, used, and torn down mid-training) is the closest in *shape* to our 2k–8k demolition, and the induction-head formation window is the canonical antecedent for watched formation of a specific circuit (MEMORY, from general knowledge, not the committed sources). What none of them do, and we did: take one named structure with a quantitative theory attached, pre-register the fossil-versus-drift fork, and classify its *properties separately*.

## "Crispness ends where training pressure ends" — meaning and provenance

(Your quote flipped a word — the claim is that crispness ends where the pressure ends.) Meaning: the model distinguishes count 37 from count 38 only within the range its training data made exact counting *pay*. The Pile's hard-wrapped text — the corpus's main incentive to count — has lines of about 70–72 characters, so predicting a newline requires exact counting up to ~70 and never beyond; past 70 there is almost no gradient rewarding exactness, and the representation there is coarse ("roughly two-thirds along the line") rather than crisp.

How we found it, step by step: a post-phase reader question on the second rung asked whether fine resolution had ever actually been measured inside the trusted range; the next seed added a recorded-only diagnostic — within each 35-count bin at width 140, the Pearson correlation between the probe's predicted count and the true count. The larger model read 0.646 / 0.820 / 0.211 / 0.227 across bins 1–35, 36–70, 71–105, 106–140; on completely fresh text the next rung read 0.650 / 0.830 / 0.198 / 0.244 — the collapse after bin two replicated to two decimals. The corpus-side number (~70–72 characters, from the verified source table) was committed *before* either measurement. Honesty bounds, unchanged: the alignment of those two numbers is correlational — the causal test (train on differently wrapped corpora) is named in the proposal's tiers and unrun — and the smaller model complicates the simple story: same corpus, same pressure, no fine structure at all, so pressure explains *where* the edge sits but not *whether* the fine structure forms. That last part took the formation sweep to see: the boundary is the final thing built, at 45% of training, and only at the scale that builds it at all.
